A within-subjects crossover experiment with 24 participants compared the redesign against its predecessor. Perceived usability rose from 77.3 to 85.0 on the System Usability Scale. Actionability gained most among the explanation-quality items, the aspect both earlier studies flagged as weakest, and the odds of a correct remediation were 2.6 times higher. Triage accuracy and time per finding were indistinguishable, which we read as uninformative rather than as equivalence. Trust was the one measure that did not move, and the closing interviews indicate that grounding made findings easier to understand rather than easier to believe. Participants also drew a boundary no requirement anticipated, wanting the tool to find and explain while they judge and apply.

papers.title: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for Rényi orders $α\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

papers.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
papers.abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $π_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

papers.title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
papers.abstract: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.

papers.title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
papers.abstract: This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices. We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.

papers.title: CapBuddy: Efficient Physical Memory Management for Capability-based Resource-controlling Microkernel
papers.abstract: Capability-based resource-controlling microkernels securely multiplex hardware by exposing low-level resource abstractions guarded by capability systems. Such a design helps provide an application-specific resource management policy to achieve high performance without sacrificing security. However, the misuse of capability-protected secure abstractions can introduce performance overhead in user-level resource management, affecting the runtime performance of dynamic applications in emerging scenarios. In this paper, we focus on the secure abstraction of physical memory in microkernels with capability-based resource management delegation to investigate an appropriate design for dynamic memory management. We propose CapBuddy, an approach to building an efficient buddy system on capability-protected secure abstractions of memory, to bypass the performance overhead of the capability system by offloading functionalities that can run offline from the critical path of serving a memory request. We implemented a prototype system on the seL4 library OS, and the evaluation results show that our approach improves the performance of the seL4 user-level buddy system by 20 to 54.5 times and achieves the same order of magnitude as Linux. Further burst experiments evaluate CapBuddy's scalability and show that it maintains low median allocation latency as the number of concurrent clients increases.

papers.title: The Ordinary Days of Extraordinary Blazar 3C 454.3
papers.abstract: The blazar 3C 454.3 (z = 0.859) is one of the brightest and most variable flat-spectrum radio quasars in the sky. Here, we present a multi-wavelength analysis of this enigmatic object in its quiescent states during June 2022 and May 2023 coincident with its first X-ray polarimetric and hard X-ray observations with International X-ray Polarimetric Explorer (IXPE) and Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array (NuSTAR). Though no X-ray polarization was detected, NuSTAR detected the source on all occasions during this period. We generated five broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs)of the blazar using quasi-simultaneous observations taken with the Fermi-Large Area Telescope, NuSTAR, and Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. The hard X-ray flux measured by NuSTAR exhibited mild flux variations. The SEDs were modeled with a one-zone leptonic emission framework using the JetSet package. The optical-ultraviolet spectrum of 3C 454.3 revealed an upturn which we reproduced with the standard accretion disk model. The X-ray to gamma-ray spectrum of 3C 454 was found to be well explained by the external Compton (EC) process with the seed photons provided by the BLR and accretion disk. These results provide intriguing clues about the multi-wavelength behavior of 3C 454.3 during its quiescent activity state.

papers.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

papers.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
papers.abstract: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

papers.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
papers.abstract: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.

papers.title: Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays
papers.abstract: We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials. These results yield explicit resonance criteria, bifurcation conditions, and Rabinowitz type and Fadell-Rabinowitz type alternatives for $\mathbb{R} $-distinct solutions.

papers.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $π_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference latency from 137.25 to 93.25 ms, achieving a $1.47\times$ speedup with an average success rate of 61%, compared with 60% for the unpruned baseline. Together, these results support APS-VLA as a modular, plug-in framework for efficient robotic control across VLA architectures, preserving the underlying policy parameters and native action-generation procedure.

papers.title: Artifact Filtering versus Artifact-Compensated Training in JPEG to JPEG AI Recompression
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of recompression of images from JPEG to JPEG AI format. We show that direct recompression from JPEG to JPEG~AI trained on uncompressed images is accompanied by the preservation of the JPEG image artifacts in the resulting JPEG~AI image. In order to avoid it, we evaluate an approach where an artifacts removal neural network is first applied to the input JPEG image as an external pre-filter. However, in this case, the processing time is increased by 29 times. Therefore, we propose an artifact-compensated training for JPEG AI and show that it is able to combine pre-filtering against target distortions with efficient compression without increase in the processing time.

papers.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

papers.title: TypedInk: Knowing When Not To Draw
papers.abstract: Can a scientific figure generator know when it does not have enough evidence to draw? Complete-source illustrators map a finished methodology section to a schematic, or a table to plotting code, and are never asked this question because their input is assumed complete. The research record is rarely that complete: an outline, a draft paragraph, a table, or a one-sentence intent, in any combination, and painting measured numbers with an image model when the table is missing is a hallucinated result. TypedInk infers a figure type from {diagram, plot, plate} from a possibly incomplete source and dispatches to the renderer that can honor that type's evidence contract, refusing dispatch when the contract cannot be met. On the six gold plots in TypedFigBench (5 views, n=30), TypedInk's code path inks every gold table token when a table is observed (12/12), refuses the 12 hidden-table views instead of inventing numbers, and marks 6 intent-only views illustrative, with no execution failures. An always-draw coder with no such gate inks 30/30 charts, including all 18 with no table, and recovers zero gold numbers on any of them; two vision-language raters (not humans; human replication is future work) still judge those always-draw charts submittable 17/36 times, against TypedInk's refusal 0/36 times. A diagnostic field ablation of the type router (16 illustrations, 5 views each, n=80) locates where this failure would originate if unchecked: an outline alone yields type accuracy 0.31 and sends every gold plot into an integrity violation, and a chat-model planner narrows but does not close the gap (overall accuracy 0.85, still integrity-failing on 25% of outlines). Diagram-label recall is 0.47 on the full record and 0.19 on an outline. Gold plates are typed at dispatch (oracle integrity-fail 0.00) and rendered as stills.

papers.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly receive UI screenshots as part of bug reports, yet degraded image quality - caused by low resolution, compression artifacts, or small rendered text - can prevent them from identifying the relevant UI elements and source files. Vision-language models become less reliable as image quality deteriorates, while OCR-assisted approaches may propagate recognition errors from degraded inputs. Both approaches are limited when the visual evidence required for localization is no longer clearly observable in the query screenshot. We propose augmenting coding agents with repository-rendered reference images: crisp screenshots generated from the same codebase that the agent is tasked with modifying. These references provide readable visual evidence of the application's UI while preserving the current, potentially bug-containing implementation state. Because they are generated from the available repository rather than requiring a known bug-free version, they can be produced automatically for reproducible application states without manual image annotation. We evaluate the approach on a controlled benchmark derived from SWE-bench Multimodal by injecting visual UI bugs into a real web application. We vary screenshot degradation and reference-image provision and measure whether the coding agent identifies the correct source file. The results show that reference images improve file localization especially for degraded image quality, increasing the gold file match rate under fourfold downsampling with JPEG compression. We confirmed with further analysis that the proposed approach recognizes text approximately 12 percentage points better than language biased OCR under the same degradation.

papers.title: Representations of the Loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a new family of non-weight modules $Ω(λ,ζ,α,β,γ,σ, h)$ over the loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra $\mathcal{G}$, which is a Takiff-type extension of the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra. We establish criteria for irreducibility, determine their isomorphism classes, and classify all $\mathcal{G}$-modules that are free of rank one. Moreover, we determine all self-extensions of these modules: for every such module $M$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{U(\mathcal{G})}(M,M)\cong \mathbb{C}^{6}$, and we construct explicit $1$-cocycles realizing every cohomology class. Every nonsplit self-extension of a simple module is indecomposable of composition length two. Restricting these modules to the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro subalgebra $\mathcal{H}$ yields new $\mathcal{H}$-modules. Among them the $σ$-type modules $Ψ(λ,ζ,σ,α,β,γ,h)$ constitute a new family with no counterpart in the non-loop or non-Takiff case. For the degenerate case $σ=0$, we establish criteria for irreducibility and isomorphism, and describe certain maximal submodules and their simple quotients. Finally, we construct and classify a new class of tensor product $\mathcal{H}$-modules.

papers.title: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs
papers.abstract: As LLMs increasingly mediate everyday interactions, subtle gender biases in open-ended responses pose growing societal risks. Existing probing methods have two key limitations: they rely on fixed-format tasks, such as pronoun resolution or occupation association, that alignment-tuned models can easily handle; and they compare raw group-level rubric scores, ignoring per-dimension variance and obscuring which bias dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups. We introduce GRAP (Gender Rubric-Aware Probing), a framework that uses a lightweight logistic probe to identify the most discriminative bias dimensions from responses scored across 10 rubric dimensions, operating task-agnostically on open-ended instruction following.

papers.title: Multi-TeV vector dark matter in the $U(1)_X$ Higgs portal model
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-mass vector dark matter within the framework of the $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal vector model, by jointly integrating experimental constraints from relic density measurements, direct detection searches, and indirect detection observations alongside the perturbative criterion to derive bounds on the model parameter space. Within the weakly interacting massive particle scenario, we assess the relative contributions of $s$-channel and $t/u$-channel processes to thermal dark matter annihilation. For parameter configurations lying in the $s$-channel resonance region, each fixed value of the scalar mixing angle $\sinα$ corresponds to a well-defined upper limit on the heavy dark scalar mass $m_{h_2}$. This upper limit decreases monotonically with increasing $\sinα$, with a critical threshold of $\sinα\lesssim 0.05$ beyond which perturbative constraints entirely exclude the full resonance corridor. By contrast, the non-resonant parameter regime dominated by $t/u$-channel annihilation processes is found to be excluded for $m_V \simeq 1$ TeV and above under the combined joint constraints from relic density requirements and perturbative consistency. Our results indicate that the perturbative consistency of the scalar sector, enforced via the two-loop renormalisation group equations, imposes bounds on the parameter space in the heavy mass regime that are comparable to, and in some benchmark regions more restrictive than, current experimental limits. Nevertheless, even under the application of these stringent perturbativity constraints, the model still admits a viable set of parameter points spanning a broad multi-TeV mass range.

papers.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
papers.abstract: AI systems can produce reliable results without developing human understanding. However, human understanding remains valuable for shaping subsequent AI-supported work, forming preferences, governing collective choices and satisfying curiosity, even when human participation is unnecessary for correcting errors. We propose understanding-first AI engineering, which treats purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle guiding requirements, design and operation. The purposes of understanding are organised into four complementary rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance and epistemic value. A reference architecture connects production, verification, use, and learning and exploration through shared records, supporting understanding through explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns guide choices about parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, audience-specific views and distributed expertise. Qualitative scenario analysis of two hypothetical use cases demonstrates how the purpose classification, reference architecture and selected patterns guide investigation, participation and decision processes while retaining operational controls. The cases illustrate design consequences and limitations rather than establish empirical effectiveness. The approach makes human understanding an explicit engineering commitment whose justification need not depend on improving the original AI task.

papers.title: Cluster-weighted modeling for count data with excess zeros and mixed-type covariates
papers.abstract: Count data may exhibit excess zeros, within-group overdispersion, and heterogeneous relationships between the response and its covariates. Conventional zero-inflated regression models typically impose a single count-regression structure, whereas Poisson count components cannot accommodate residual within-component overdispersion. We propose a zero-inflated negative binomial cluster-weighted model that combines a structural-zero component with multiple negative binomial regression components and jointly models the response and mixed-type covariates.We establish sufficient conditions for identifiability of the proposed model and its Poisson counterpart and develop an expectation-maximization algorithm for estimation. Numerical studies demonstrate improved regression coefficient estimation and clustering performance relative to the Poisson counterpart under within-component overdispersion.

papers.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
papers.abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) workflows remain highly fragmented, requiring engineers to coordinate heterogeneous representations, specialised software tools, and iterative verification across multiple design stages. Although large language models have brought more general reasoning and code-generation capabilities to EDA, many existing approaches remain focused on isolated tasks and struggle to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously within executable engineering environments. Here we introduce ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving AI agent framework for EDA. ChipOmni integrates multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction into a unified autonomous system. By continually incorporating feedback from external engineering tools, the framework maintains an evolving task context, integrates domain knowledge, and iteratively refines intermediate designs. Across benchmarks for analog circuit, RTL, testbench, and formal-assertion generation, ChipOmni improves multiple task-specific measures over the evaluated baselines and solves all 30 AnalogCoder-Pro tasks. In a long-horizon case study, ChipOmni advances a natural-language RISC-V specification through three design levels to a micro-SoC GDSII layout that passes physical sign-off, without human intervention after initialization. Together, these results show that ChipOmni can coordinate verification-driven design across heterogeneous tasks and sustain long-horizon engineering workflows, advancing a shift from fragmented, tool-centred processes towards agent-centred, closed-loop systems.

papers.title: Two-Tier Task Offloading for Satellite-Assisted Marine Networks: A Hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining Game Approach
papers.abstract: The proliferation of maritime activities has spurred the emergence of numerous computation-intensive and delay-sensitive marine applications and services. Given the inherent rationality, selfish nature, and limited computational abilities of marine devices, devising effective strategies to incentivize their participation in task processing become a critical challenge. In this paper, we investigate the satellite-assisted marine multi-access edge computing (MEC) and propose a two-tier task offloading scheme through a hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining game approach to enhance offloading efficiency and maximize the utility of marine devices. Specifically, for the underwater acoustic communication, we consider the scenario where multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), managed by maritime autonomous surface ships (MASSs), upload their collected data using non-orthogonal multiple access(NOMA) to optimize channel utilization. For the data transmission above the sea surface, we consider the scenario where a low earth orbit satellite (LEOS) functions as a space edge server to provide computing services, and MASS offloads workloads to LEOS through frequency division multiple access(FDMA) to prevent co-channel interference. we define the utility of AUVs, MASSs and LEOSs, and model the offloading process between AUVs and MASSs as a Stackelberg game, while representing the offloading interaction between MASSs and LEOSs as a Bargaining game. Additionally, we propose efficient algorithms to optimize AUV offloading strategies and MASS pricing strategies, while refining the bidding strategies for both MASSs and LEOSs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform benchmark schemes in achieving optimal solutions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension
papers.abstract: In 1999, Ashbaugh formulated the conjecture that the ball maximizes the ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean space. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$ by constructing smooth connected domains with finitely many interior holes. The key observation is that a zero-value constraint on a concentric sphere close to the boundary of a ball increases the first two eigenvalues by the same relative amount to first order, whereas their ratio increases strictly at second order. A quantitative surface penalty and logarithmic cutoffs transfer this strict inequality to smooth perforated domains. The construction gives explicit geometric parameters depending only on the dimension \(d\).

papers.title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Block drafters such as DFlash draft a block of future tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees such as DDTree verify the prefixes ranked highest by the product of the drafter's per-position distributions. Under tree verification, the expected number of accepted tokens is the probability mass the tree covers. We show that a product misallocates it: when the continuation can follow several futures, it splices them into chimeras, prefixes stitched together from different futures that the target never produces, and gives them as much budget as the futures themselves. Barring ties, no product-ranked tree can hold two futures that disagree in $m$ positions without $2^{m-1}-1$ chimeras, however well the drafter is trained, and in practice chimeras make up 27-33% of a 64-node tree. We propose Multi-Future Drafting (MFD), which restores the coupling with a latent variable instead of the chain rule: $K$ learned mode embeddings at the drafter's input draft $K$ coherent blocks in the same pass, and a mixture DDTree lets the verifier pick the future the target takes, losslessly and with $K+1$ extra vectors. On four Qwen targets from 4B to 27B parameters, at batch size 1, MFD reaches up to 7.8$\times$ speedup, 5-8% faster than the best single-mode tree trained identically and, on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, 9-16% faster than the released DARTree trained on the same prompts.

papers.title: Permutation-Based Pre-trained Model Merging via Reciprocal Orthogonality
papers.abstract: Ito et al. (2026) showed that sufficiently wide, independently trained neural networks can exhibit linear mode connectivity (LMC) with softmax temperature calibration, even without permutation. LMC means that a low-loss linear path connects the models' parameters. This behavior is explained by layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity (LEWC), whereby each merged layer outputs an exponentially weighted sum of the original models' corresponding representations, yielding ensemble-like predictions. However, prior work observed LEWC with substantial widening, such as 8192 units per hidden layer for MLPs and $16\times$ width for VGG-11, raising the question of whether such widths are necessary. We therefore search for permutations that encourage reciprocal orthogonality (RO), which suppresses interference between each model's weights and the other model's representations. This allows both models' computations to coexist in the merged network, promoting LEWC at smaller widths. We formulate the search as independent layerwise quadratic assignment problems and approximately solve their continuous relaxations using Frank--Wolfe. Experiments show that our method facilitates LMC with less width expansion. It also merges models trained on different data distributions, where weight matching, which maximizes weight similarity through permutations, struggles. The merged predictions approximate those of a logit ensemble of the original models.

papers.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

papers.title: Is a CNN-Transformer Ensemble Worth It When a Chest X-Ray Foundation Model Is Available?
papers.abstract: Ensembles of ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks and Vision Transformers are a common way to improve multi-label chest X-ray classification. We ask whether such an ensemble is still worth its cost when a model pretrained on chest radiographs is available. On the official patient-disjoint split of NIH ChestX-ray14 (25,596 test images, 2,797 patients), we train five ImageNet-pretrained backbones and the EVA-X-S foundation model with validation-only model selection, compare five fusion rules, and estimate every difference with a patient-level paired bootstrap. EVA-X-S alone reached a test macro-AUROC of 0.828; the five-model ensemble reached 0.814 (difference -0.0136, 95% CI -0.0178 to -0.0098) at about 7.8 times the summed backbone latency and ten times the parameters. Averaging the five ImageNet models with EVA-X-S changed AUROC by -0.0056 (-0.0095 to -0.0021). With all five ImageNet backbones trained with the EVA-X-S recipe, their ensemble scored 0.817, still -0.0109 (-0.0142 to -0.0076) below EVA-X-S, and across three seeds EVA-X-S varied by at most 0.001 AUROC. Under the ImageNet models' recipe, however, EVA-X-S fell to 0.798. Our full-stacking configuration never outperformed calibrated averaging. In this setting, the tested ImageNet ensembles did not improve on a single chest X-ray foundation model fine-tuned with its own recipe.

papers.title: FaST: Factored Synthesis of Transitions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. We present FaST (Factored Synthesis of Transitions), which factors transitions via the chain rule into state, action, dynamics, reward, and terminal stages, fitting each with an estimator matched to its statistical properties. Across twelve D4RL locomotion and maze benchmarks, TD3+BC and IQL agents trained on FaST transitions match the SynthER diffusion baseline while generating transitions over 90x faster. The explicit action-given-state conditional can also be re-queried for a fixed state, enabling targeted action synthesis: drawing N candidate actions per generated state and keeping the highest-advantage one under a value function fit to the same data, thereby synthesizing improved behavior during generation rather than filtering for it post-hoc. Best-of-10 synthesis beats training on real data on 11 of 12 medium and medium-replay settings (+8.9 D4RL points on average, up to +28.4), and is competitive with advantage-filtered SynthER at a fraction of its generation cost. On expert mixtures both mechanisms degrade identically, tracing the failure to the advantage estimate itself rather than to either targeting mechanism.

papers.title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter
papers.abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. Existing tools primarily reproduce the word-level conventions of corpora such as BEST; however, because the notion of a "word" in Thai lacks a unified linguistic consensus, these conventions struggle with productive compounding, leading to arbitrary boundaries and ambiguity in downstream representations. Instead, we propose operating at the morphological level, focusing on khammoon, the smallest atomic unit that carries meaning. Segmenting at the morphemic level provides an explicit, consistent morphological representation that eliminates compounding ambiguity. Crucially, this representation benefits downstream learning: models trained on morphemes perform on par with or exceed word-level baselines across part-of-speech tagging, named-entity recognition, and sentiment classification, demonstrating that linguistic consistency improves representation quality without downstream performance penalty. To operationalize this representation, we translate linguistic principles into a formal decision guideline with near-perfect human agreement ($κ\approx 0.99$), scale annotation with an LLM, and correct systematic errors with human labels. Finally, we train khammoon, a lightweight 1M-parameter convolutional BiLSTM segmenter designed for efficient CPU inference, achieving a boundary F1 of 0.992 on out-of-domain text. The guideline, datasets, model, and library are all publicly released.

papers.title: Compile-Gated Lean Proof Refactoring with Enterprise Agent Practices: A Model per Step under a US\$3 Cap, Followed by Programmatic Rewrite Rules
papers.abstract: Our closed-track entry (Arena username Vexorium-Agent) scored 86.31 points on the final board (L = 77.07, H = 81.86, Z = 100) over the 60 final problems, against 33.33 for the reference proofs, 8th at the deadline (top: 92.57), for US\$166.33 at list prices with every call counted (per problem: mean US\$2.772, at most US\$2.874; US\$3 cap). Three practices carry the entry. First, each paid stage runs the model that measured best per dollar for it among the 9 we tested in our own harness: GPT-6.1 Sol the early sessions, GPT-6.1 Terra the later ones and the tail at 70% of Sol's cost per turn, and Gemini 4 Argon the review and repair; Sol also runs the style rewrite. Second, what our development and research runs learned ships as compiler-checked programmatic rewrite rules rather than prompt text (+0.93 points from rules fixed before the release; +0.26 and +0.30, in sample, from passes built or switched on after the release). Third, every call is recorded and reviewed before each change (all 9 board scores came within -0.063 to +0.015 points of our meter's prediction). The harness, gate and many of these rules also serve our open-track entry. We report the full bill and the spread of three runs.

papers.title: Preserving Cultural Records: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Visual-Prior Routing Network for Ancient Book Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Ancient books preserve invaluable cultural heritage, yet their images often suffer from complex degradations caused by long-term ageing, environmental exposure, and physical damage. Existing ancient book image restoration benchmarks are limited in scale and rely on simplified degradation simulations, which cannot fully represent real-world degradation patterns and restrict the generalization ability of restoration models. To address these challenges, we introduce AncBench, a large-scale synthetic paired benchmark containing 100K aligned clean-degraded image pairs. AncBench models realistic composite degradations through a comprehensive degradation pipeline that considers material ageing, paper texture variation, blur, staining, water-induced geometric distortion, and local occlusion. Furthermore, we propose AncRestore, a degradation-aware visual-prior routing network for ancient book image restoration. AncRestore first learns degradation representations from degraded images and then dynamically selects and integrates suitable visual priors according to different degradation characteristics. Guided by these degradation cues, a dynamic routing mechanism combines expert-wise and region-wise routing strategies adaptively adjusts the contribution of these priors across different regions, enabling the model to recover both global appearance and local text details. Extensive experiments show that AncRestore effectively suppresses composite degradations while preserving text structures and enhancing restoration quality against other methods, highlighting its application potential for intelligent ancient book image restoration in cultural heritage preservation.

papers.title: Instance-preserving graded semantic reporting for surgical action triplets
papers.abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. We introduce instance-preserving graded semantic reporting, which separates instance selection from the choice of semantic detail. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. The utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost. We compare three decision rules on 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos using fixed predictions and scores. At the 10% development calibration target, DELTA retains correct partial reports for 80.0% of candidates rejected by a matched complete-or-reject baseline (5,329/6,662). Adding IV increases source-normalized weighted correct-report yield by 19.13 to 23.13 per 100 frames across all three rules relative to separately recalibrated I/IVT controls. Weighted reporting risk changes by -0.77 to +1.01 percentage points, with complete correct-triplet counts unchanged or reduced. Graded reporting makes partial surgical predictions available as localized descriptions, with an explicit trade-off between report utility and completeness.

papers.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
papers.abstract: The author describes an open implementation flow, from HDL to a programmable bitstream, for the Xilinx Spartan-3E (XC3S100E to XC3S1200E) and Spartan-6 (XC6SLX16, XC6SLX45), devices that only the discontinued ISE 14.7 supports. The flow runs unchanged in a web browser or in Node.js: Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, with nextpnr's Himbaechel framework given Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 architectures generated from Silinx's own device descriptions, bit database and timing model, and Silinx's own bitstream writer. The bit database was built by black-box observation of ISE's documented XDL and bitgen tools, using codeword-batched experiments; the router is given only switches whose bits were measured, and the writer refuses a feature it has not measured. ISE is the oracle: for the same placed and routed design, the bitstream is byte-identical to the one bitgen writes and ISE's DRC is clean. Placement and routing were first done by an in-house annealer and PathFinder router, which nextpnr replaced once it matched them. On 67 open-source designs for the XC3S1200E, compared with ISE at the same optimisation goal (45 designs built by both), the flow uses 15% fewer slices and has 14% shorter critical paths at goal Area, 21% fewer slices and 8% shorter paths at Speed, and 20% fewer slices but 12% longer paths at Fast (geometric means). XST cannot read 15 of the designs. The flow is published as the npm package silinx-fpga (Apache-2.0).

papers.title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes consequential decisions, yet predictive accuracy is not a sufficient justification for delegated authority. This conceptual study develops an integrated framework for assessing just AI across normative, data, model, and governance layers. Drawing on plural theories of justice, sociotechnical fairness research, and publicly available governance standards, it maps six justice requirements to observable evidence, decision rights, and remedies. It proposes a two-stage evaluation rule: exclude uses that fail independently justified minimum rights constraints, then compare eligible alternatives across multiple performance and governance criteria. As an explicitly limited normative analogy, Genesis chapter 2 motivates a Forbidden-Boundary Principle (FBP), under which an AI agent must not execute externally consequential actions outside pre-authorized boundaries. The resulting First-Principle Safe-Stop Protocol (FPSSP) comprises an independently governed policy monitor, a mandatory execution gate, a restricted or alternative safe-state controller, immutable-oriented audit trails, and accountable human authorization for recovery. We distinguish this normative and traceability contribution from existing Simplex and runtime assurance architectures; we do not claim a novel safety switch or formal proof of universal ethical compliance. A policy schema, threat model, test matrix, outcome definitions, and a prospective comparison design make the proposal falsifiable. No FPSSP implementation, experimental dataset, numerical improvement, or verified latency bound is reported. The framework supports future evaluation rather than constituting evidence of operational safety.

papers.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism. On 507 internal cases across five imaging types, MedScope-4B reached ESG 0.758 and claimed an erased lesion in 9.6% of cases, against 0.27-0.47 and 41-62% for the frontier models (all p<0.001), without significant loss of accuracy on real lesions. Without counterfactual views ESG fell to 0.279+-0.107 (three seeds); the effect replicated on MedGemma 1.5 4B and two unseen inpainting tools. At four external centres the advantage held but frontier models detected more real lesions; on a fresh external test MedScope-4B detected 0 of 48 pneumothorax films, with net utility below gemini-4-argon's (-0.36 [-0.50, -0.23]). Matching the control edit was not shown to matter; over three seeds no fresh-external ESG advantage over removal-based DPO was established; a paired-view consistency objective did not beat a matched-compute control, while that continuation alone cut erased-lesion claims on unseen tools at every seed, at a cost in sensitivity at one. Training on erased and edited images gives a small model an evidence-gated disposition that prompting does not give frontier models; it does not improve perception, and rare critical findings need coverage.

papers.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
papers.abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. We turn this into a bootstrapping procedure that exposes redundancy in the ground-truth supervision without any external oracle, which we demonstrate on redundancy-injected versions of our datasets. Finally, the log-signature encoder induces a markedly more interpretable latent geometry than the baselines, in which the nearest neighbors of every state lie on its own execution trace.

papers.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
papers.abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution, our model delivers a \(20\times\) speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

papers.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. Branching provides no benefit in low-dispersion settings, while increasing return by 12.8% in our main Craftax-Medium setting. Most of this gain comes not from selecting better actions, but from selecting among different stochastic realizations of the same action. Several competent verifiers achieve similar episode returns, suggesting that verifier quality is not the main constraint at our operating budget. Instead, computation is better allocated to states where useful dispersion is likely. On held-out seeds, gating branching using predicted dispersion retains 69% of the improvement from uniform branching while using 48% as many branching calls. These results characterize when branch-and-commit is useful and clarify what its gains represent.

papers.title: YTShorts-92K: An Interpretable Multimodal Dataset of YouTube Shorts
papers.abstract: Short-form video has become one of the dominant formats of online content, yet large-scale datasets enabling the analysis of what makes these videos successful remain limited. Existing resources often focus on post-publication popularity signals or rely on non-interpretable representations such as high-dimensional embeddings. Here, we introduce YTShorts-92K, a dataset of 92,654 YouTube Shorts collected from 345 creators and spanning 12 manually defined content categories. Each video is enriched with an interpretable multimodal feature set covering metadata, textual information, visual characteristics from frames and thumbnails, and cross-modal consistency measures. We describe the collection methodology, data cleaning process, and feature extraction pipeline, followed by descriptive analyses of the diversity of creators, topics, and extracted features. This dataset offers a reusable resource for studying short-form video content, online attention, and multimodal content analysis.

papers.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
papers.abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (\ours{}), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. We compare task ranks on aligned support, train five backbones under all seven non-empty objective combinations on five datasets with three seeds, and contrast fixed-model profiles with specialist portfolios. Rank comparisons connect imputation and prediction through numerical recovery and dependence preservation, and link generation to both through predictive utility; distributional fidelity follows different, sometimes opposing, rankings. Objective interventions show the largest pooled gains from including the recipient's own objective. Generation has the broadest coverage of positive pooled auxiliary effects, while prediction shows potential to improve imputation and synthetic-data utility, with responses that vary across backbones. Cross-addition effects reveal that objective benefits need not add and depend on the objectives already present. Fixed-model comparisons expose corresponding utility--fidelity trade-offs: some generalists surpass specialist portfolios on utility, while fidelity continues to favor specialization. Frozen foundation models show strong prediction and numerical point imputation, together with promising synthetic-data utility, highlighting their potential across all three tasks. These findings motivate unified tabular models that share useful conditional information while improving categorical reconstruction and faithful joint sampling.

papers.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
papers.abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

papers.title: Direct Multispectral Satellite Nowcasting of Gridded Surface Solar Radiation
papers.abstract: Surface shortwave radiation (SWR) can change within minutes as clouds evolve, but operational forecasts often trade spatial detail and update frequency for forecast range. We present a numerical-weather-prediction-independent, observation-to-forecast framework that converts sequences of Himawari-8 Level-1 multispectral imagery and solar geometry directly into 24 gridded SWR fields at 10-min intervals for the next 4 h. A controlled six-model experiment separates the effects of satellite information from those of temporal self-attention. In the 0-1 h window, the full-multispectral attention model achieves a mean absolute error of 37.9 W/m2 and a root mean square error of 63.7 W/m2, reductions of 21.0% and 19.5% relative to a historical-SWR baseline. Improvements extend across nine subregions and include weaker spatial bias and better structural consistency. Temporal attention does not improve forecasts from historical SWR alone, but becomes effective when supplied with multispectral cloud and thermodynamic signals. Direct multispectral observations therefore provide the precursor information required for high-frequency, spatially resolved SWR nowcasting.

papers.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. These are (1) that the concept is decodable from the activations, (2) that they form a specific shape, (3) that the shape belongs to the probed concept rather than to a related concept the model also represents, and (4) that the output of the model depends on the shape. We call these claims decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use, and we test them separately with a four-stage Bayesian pipeline. Stage 2 compares candidate shapes and selects the best one only when its evidence passes a predefined threshold. Stage 3 removes a set of related concepts, specified in advance, and tests whether the shape is owned or inherited. Stage 4 intervenes on the shape to test whether the output of the model depends on it. We apply the pipeline to two-digit addition and multiplication in GPT-J 6B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Pythia 6.9B. Nearly every concept is decodable, but the decoded directions overlap substantially across concepts. Every strongly supported comparison selects a ribbon, which is a helix whose radius changes with the value, or a torus. Of 1,330 cells with an ownership verdict, 19% of shapes are owned and 81% are inherited. Owned and inherited shapes move the output about equally often. Intervening on the shape retains approximately 61% of the effect of intervening on the full probe while using at most five dimensions, against a median of nine for the probe. Our results indicate that a probe verdict alone overstates what a model computes with, and we propose that probe results be reported as verdicts on all four claims rather than as a single accuracy.

papers.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
papers.abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives exhibit a structural limitation: by assuming equal reliability across all proxy supervision signals, they induce posterior over-contraction and forced explanations. To address this issue, we propose TIB, a sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck framework that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, while also validating the identified failure mode.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
papers.abstract: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For $r=2$, subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every $r\ge3$, we construct a family with $2r+12$ triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree $2r+1$. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.

papers.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components. With fewer extraneous tentacles, each edit affects less other knowledge, enabling better coexistence. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmark datasets verify the effectiveness of our method. Code: https://github.com/wintersdragon-c/STO.

papers.title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(γ,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $γ$-Process Calculations
papers.abstract: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $γ$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. The photon flux and energy distribution were determined with a LaBr$3$(Ce) spectrometer, and monoenergetic cross sections were obtained using an iterative unfolding method. Below 12~MeV, the present cross sections agree well with the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluations. However, near the maximum of the $(γ,n)$ excitation function, the present cross sections are significantly higher than both the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluated values. The $E1$ $γ$-ray strength functions were derived by fitting the experimental cross sections measured at SLEGS and NewSUBARU. The stellar reaction rates for $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ and $^{168}\mathrm{Tm}(n,γ)$ were calculated by incorporating these constrained $γ$-ray strength functions into the TALYS code. The calculated $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ rates were adopted in a full $p$-process reaction network for the shock-heated O/Ne-rich layers of a $20 M\odot$ core-collapse supernova model to perform a sensitivity analysis. The updated rates have a negligible effect on the final $p$-nucleus abundances.

papers.title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
papers.abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

papers.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model
papers.abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. We propose ZeroPoint, an EBM that makes the empty answer a state of the model with energy zero for every input. This fixed state provides an explicit reference for the energies of all listed options, whose non-negative depths measure their compatibility with the input relative to the empty answer. The options and the empty answer share one distribution, in which an option at zero depth receives no probability. The decision to select an option or to abstain is thus part of ordinary inference, trained with the negative log-likelihood loss, rather than a separate rejection rule. The energy function is a small multilingual encoder that reads the input together with all the options and is invariant to their order. Ablations show that most of the benefit comes from training with examples in which no option fits. With the same encoder and data, the fixed zero separates inputs with and without an acceptable option slightly better than a learned rejection class and clearly better than a thresholded softmax, while leaving the choice among options unchanged.

papers.title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
papers.abstract: Given the discrete nature of many software engineering (SE) optimization problems, trapping at local optima remains a crucial issue in the optimizer designs. Meta Multi-Objectivization (MMO) is an optimization model for overcoming local optima by introducing an extra, auxiliary objective. Yet, MMO is originally designed only for configuration tuning, leaving its suitability for other SE problems in doubt, particularly regarding the choice of the auxiliary objective. In this paper, we study the possibility and resolution for specializing MMO as a general baseline across a range of SE optimization problems, making it a fundamental counterpart for future SE optimizers that seek to mitigate the issue of local optima. We do so by providing both theoretical remit and empirical evidence: we analytically show how the choice of the auxiliary objective is crucial while demonstrating the effectiveness of MMO under nine SE optimization problems comprising 212 cases when the right one can be chosen, i.e., MMO is able to outperform the other state-of-the-art and general-purpose optimizers in 79% and 94% of the cases, respectively. Drawing on the theoretical understanding and empirical findings, we then propose L2RAC, a tool that automatically recommends the best auxiliary objective choice for a given SE problem/case, hence helping to specialize MMO therein. Through extensive experiments, we reveal that, in general, L2RAC can more accurately rank the choice of auxiliary objective for MMO under a case than other guesses by up to 60%, saving as much as 99% of the cost that would otherwise be required to conduct trial-and-error when using MMO.

papers.title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers
papers.abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing, while foundation-model-centric methods pretrain transferable multimodal graph encoders or bring graph context into multimodal large language models for prediction and generation. In parallel, several benchmarks have appeared with different datasets and evaluation protocols. This survey takes an algorithm-centric and evaluation-grounded view of the field and makes three contributions. Modeling: we introduce a unified message-passing formulation and organize methods into five integration levels (feature, propagation, topology, learning, and foundation model), covering discriminative and graph-conditioned generative models; within this formulation we derive representative methods as special cases, compare their assumptions, expressiveness, and cost, and identify cross-modal sensitivity as a property that separates otherwise similar architectures. Datasets and evaluation: we review recent benchmarks, summarize their datasets and metrics, define model-independent descriptors (label homophily, average degree, clustering, and edge provenance), and map each evaluation protocol to the baselines it uses. Frontiers: we connect multimodal graph learning to AI agents, covering the multimodal graphs that agents perceive and remember and graph engineering, the practice of organizing agent workflows as explicit graphs; we then discuss open problems, concrete efforts for the community, and research directions, including when graph structure helps in the presence of strong multimodal foundation models.

papers.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
papers.abstract: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios

papers.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update.
