papers.abstract: Robots are typically evaluated in episodes that begin from a reset, while industrial work consists of repeated jobs whose outcomes affect subsequent operations. Evaluating such work at scale requires simulation of task-critical physical interactions, construction of industrial environments, and measurements of performance as scene state persists. We present HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0, a framework for simulating, generating, and evaluating industrial robot work. Given a human-specified workplace and task, the framework defines a world pairing a scenario of scene variants and process logic with an evaluation defining a job, metrics, and a rubric. HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0 comprises three components. HOLIDAY-SIM extends Newton's SDF-based hydroelastic contact with additional constitutive laws and a semi-implicit primal-dual solver, couples stateful actuator dynamics to articulated motion, and derives tactile and joint observations from simulated states. Agentic world construction generates simulation-ready assets and scene variants using geometric and interaction checks, and proposes task-conditioned evaluations for human confirmation and executable checks. 24/7-BENCH introduces seven industrial tasks in which jobs are evaluated without resetting the scene, measuring completed, failed, and unfinished jobs, throughput, latency, and motor energy. Controlled studies characterize the proposed contact, actuator, and tactile models and examine the effectiveness of verification-guided world construction. Experiments on scene and evaluation generation further reveal the limitations of model critics and the difficulty of ensuring that generated evaluations faithfully capture task requirements. We examine job-level evaluations with scripted trajectories (e.g., code-as-policy) but have not yet compared policies over persistent runs.

papers.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=π^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $σ$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schrödinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.

papers.title: Structure-Informed Electromagnetic Feedback Control of the Vlasov-Maxwell System with Delayed Observations
papers.abstract: Feedback control of kinetic plasma instabilities is challenging because observing the full phase-space distribution is costly, while sensing and actuation inevitably introduce delay. We develop a structure-informed electromagnetic feedback framework for the Vlasov-Maxwell system that uses only macroscopic observations to control the full kinetic distribution. We first show that magnetic actuation alone does not directly regulate radial velocity moments, motivating the use of combined electric and magnetic controls. A nonlinear perturbation estimate yields an instantaneous cancellation-dissipation feedback law. To account for delayed observations, we then use Maxwell's equations to identify the macroscopic quantities governing the resulting cancellation errors, namely currents and spatial field gradients. These quantities serve as inputs to a low-rank neural operator that learns a residual correction to the delayed cancellation baseline. Thus, while the feedback depends only on low-dimensional macroscopic observables, the control objective remains the stabilization of the full distribution toward a prescribed kinetic equilibrium. Numerical experiments for two-stream and Weibel-type instabilities demonstrate effective long-time stabilization under substantial feedback delays.

papers.title: Payoff-Aware Prediction of Population Game Dynamics
papers.abstract: Population game dynamics describe how aggregate behavior evolves in response to payoff signals. In many applications, the payoff function may change, and the goal is to predict the population trajectory induced by a new payoff design before trajectory data under that design are available. We study this problem as $\textbf{payoff-aware prediction of population game dynamics}$. Standard dynamics learning methods fit the motion observed under training payoffs, but do not separate the payoff-dependent incentive from the payoff-independent response structure needed for prediction under new payoffs. Building on the existing framework of Riemannian game dynamics, we propose PA-RmD, a payoff-aware learning method that keeps payoff information explicit and learns the payoff-independent response structure from data. Theoretically, we show that the learned model preserves fixed-payoff Nash equilibria and derive finite-time one-step prediction bounds under shared-response and payoff-coverage conditions. Empirically, we evaluate PA-RmD on synthetic zero-sum and potential games, as well as a YouTube Trending multi-country dataset, showing that our method performs well under changing payoff designs.

papers.title: On the robustness of locally D-optimal designs under parameter uncertainty in single-factor generalized linear models
papers.abstract: Local and Bayesian approaches to optimal experimental design specify information about the regression parameters through a nominal value and a prior distribution, respectively. A practical question is whether accounting for parameter uncertainty justifies replacing a locally optimal design. We investigate when locally D-optimal designs remain Bayesian D-optimal in single-factor Poisson, gamma and logistic regression on the unit interval. Analytical arguments and numerical comparisons under normal and uniform slope priors examine how prior form and dispersion affect the optimal support and the Bayesian D-efficiency of retaining a local design.

papers.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
papers.abstract: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

papers.title: Fairness Drift: Assessing Algorithmic Fairness in a Moving Market
papers.abstract: Flexible models and richer data can reduce systematic valuation errors and improve fairness. Yet algorithmic values stay fixed between updates while the market moves, so a new algorithm gains most against an intact distortion and least where uneven appreciation has eroded or just reversed it. We study property assessment, which sets tax bills and has long over-assessed cheaper homes. Cook County replaced township regressions and manual adjustments with a gradient-boosted model and richer data on its triennial cycle: Chicago in 2021, northern suburbs in 2022, southern in 2023. We estimate difference-in-differences in how the assessment-to-price ratio varies with sale price and neighborhood minority share. In Chicago, the reform halved the relative over-assessment of cheaper homes and, among equally priced homes, weakened the link to neighborhood racial composition. In the suburbs the price gradient was unchanged: the North's legacy values were already accurate, and the South's cheap neighborhoods had appreciated faster under frozen values, correcting part of the distortion, then stalled in the reassessment year, leaving the new values too high where prices had gained and accuracy unimproved. Fairness thus drifts with the market between updates, and single-deployment evaluations may credit or blame the algorithm for what the market did.

papers.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models have emerged as promising paradigms for decoding brain activity through large-scale self-supervised pretraining. Notably, most existing approaches employ masked patch reconstruction, in which randomly selected EEG patches are masked and recovered by the network. However, purely random masking may limit representation learning as informative patches from highly correlated channels often remain unmasked, causing the network to underutilize weakly correlated channels or serial dependencies. Furthermore, because these models are typically based on transformer architectures, their performance is influenced by the choice of positional encoding. Although positional encoding has been extensively explored in natural language processing and computer vision, few studies have adapted it to the unique characteristics of EEG signals. To address these limitations, this study introduces a conditional positional encoding method based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to explicitly model inter-channel correlations, along with an adaptive masking strategy that enhances representation learning by modulating the difficulty of masked patch reconstruction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to integrate graph-based representations into conditional positional encoding and introduce adaptive masking within EEG foundation model pretraining. Experimental results on ten benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCN-based positional encoding and adaptive masking strategies, both individually and in combination, achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance, highlighting their effectiveness in EEG foundation modeling.

papers.title: Supercurrent-controlled magnon transport via suppression of the superconducting gap
papers.abstract: Understanding interactions between different low-energy excitations is a central theme in condensed-matter physics. Magnons and superconducting condensates represent two distinct macroscopic quantum states, yet their mutual interaction remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate supercurrent-controlled magnon transport in a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure. We observe that the magnon transport signal decreases as the supercurrent increases. This suppression originates from a supercurrent-induced reduction of the superconducting gap, which enhances magnon dissipation into the superconductor via Bogoliubov quasiparticles. Our results provide direct experimental evidence of a supercurrent-controlled interaction between magnons and quasiparticles in the superconductor. The approach used in this study relies on supercurrents, enabling magnon modulation without Joule heating. These findings establish a new route to control magnons via superconductivity and pave the way for energy-efficient magnonic devices.

papers.title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models
papers.abstract: Sampling-based planners such as MPPI and CEM query a learned world model thousands of times per control step, so low-bit world models are an obvious way to make model-based control cheaper on a robot. With round-to-nearest activation quantization and no calibration, we find that planning can collapse, by up to 100 points of success, while the world model's latent one-step prediction error stays no larger than that of a stochastic rounding scheme that plans well. At the same bit width, what decides the outcome is not the size of the rounding error but whether it persists across planner iterations and is shared across candidates. Round-to-nearest leaves an error that persists, and an iterating planner drifts toward the candidates that this error favors; in TD-MPC2, holding the same dither fixed within a step or an episode brings the drift back. Dither shared by all candidates and redrawn at every iteration removes most of the damage at the same bit width and without training: at least half of it in all 19 affected Meta-World cells (task $\times$ bit width) of TD-MPC2 (median 95%), in 4 of 5 DINO-WM cells, and in all 8 affected tasks of a 317M-parameter multi-task TD-MPC2. Captured as CUDA graphs on an Ampere GPU, a W8A4 integer TD-MPC2 world model runs its planning rollouts 1.9-3.3$\times$ and the whole planning step 1.3-1.5$\times$ faster than FP32, though not faster than BF16 with pre-converted weights; shared dither adds at most 2.3% latency. In TD-MPC2, block-scaled NVFP4 removes most of the damage and MXFP4 part of it, which ties the failure to coarse grids with a shared scale. Hypotheses, thresholds and analysis code were fixed before the data that test them, and the hypotheses that failed are reported.

papers.title: Collective Signatures of Pionic Correlations at High Momentum Transfer
papers.abstract: High-momentum-transfer reactions have provided experimental evidence for enhanced pionic correlations in nuclei, yet the microscopic connection between the low-energy pionic response and the delta-hole excitation spectrum remains unresolved. Here we identify hybrid pion-delta collective modes that emerge through the coherent coupling of nucleon-hole and delta-hole excitations. By evaluating the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the random-phase approximation, we find a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode and a higher-energy collective delta-hole mode. The low-energy mode is strongly enhanced as the Landau-Migdal parameter is reduced, exhibiting behavior characteristic of a precursor to pion condensation. We further show that these modes may be probed through high-momentum-transfer charged-pion production reactions. Because the same collective pion-delta function governs both the response and the RPA correlation energy, our results connect experimentally observable collective excitations with microscopic many-body correlations.

papers.title: Homomesy of tropical $T$-systems for pairs of simply laced Dynkin diagrams
papers.abstract: For a pair of simply laced Dynking diagrams $X$ and $X'$, we prove Chin's homomesy conjecture on the number of red and blue mutations in a period of the tropical Zamolodchikov $T$-system associated to $(X, X')$ using Nakanishi's dilogarithm identity.

papers.title: Towards Trustworthy Mobile Speech Interaction: Ensuring Voice Authenticity and Transmission Integrity
papers.abstract: The rapid progress of generative speech models has made high-fidelity voice cloning and editing cheap, fast, and widely accessible, weakening the security of voiceprint-based authentication in mobile speech interactions. Existing speech watermarking techniques focus on offline protection or watermarking synthetic speech, and thus cannot verify whether a live utterance originates from the genuine speaker at capture time. We present \textit{MoBiMark}, a real-time \textbf{mo}bile \textbf{bi}ologic speech water\textbf{mark}ing system that binds ultrasonic articulatory signatures to speech content and embeds a dynamic watermark during capture. MoBiMark emits a multi-frequency ultrasonic probe on commodity smartphones, extracts echo features from the vocal tract, and fuses them with a content-dependent speech embedding to produce a dual-layer dynamic watermark combining a persistent user identifier (UID) and a per-utterance speech identifier (SID), enabling both source authentication and propagation-time tamper detection. A jointly trained embedder and detector injects the watermark while preserving perceptual quality, and system-level optimization with INT8 quantization enables lightweight on-device deployment. Evaluated on 50 users across four smartphone models, MoBiMark achieves an average 99.79% accuracy in source and propagation attacks, with negligible impact on speech quality and intelligibility.

papers.title: Nonexistence of cusp singularities for gravity waves of extreme form
papers.abstract: In this paper we revisit the geometric approach developed by Vărvărucă and Weiss for the Stokes conjecture for gravity water waves near stagnation points, in both the irrotational and rotational settings. They introduced monotonicity formulas and frequency formulas to classify all possible singularities of solutions at stagnation points. Two questions were left open: 1. whether cusp singularities can be excluded in higher dimensions $n\geq 3$ [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]; 2. whether cusp singularities for rotational waves can be excluded under the Rayleigh-Taylor condition [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 29 (2012)]. We answer both questions in the affirmative. Our main results show that cusp singularities do not exist in higher dimensions and cannot occur for rotational waves even without assuming the Rayleigh-Taylor condition. Our argument combines a delicate analysis of the weighted volume arising from the corresponding free boundary problem with a weighted isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: Horizon-penetrating rotating black-hole configurations in VCDM
papers.abstract: A regular black-hole metric need not define a regular configuration of VCDM, whose preferred foliation is part of the gravitational solution. We construct stationary rotating, possibly charged configurations on the constant-auxiliary Einstein-Maxwell branch. Their Kerr-Newman and Kerr-Newman-de Sitter geometries carry nonzero constant-mean-curvature foliations that cross the future black-hole horizon and, in the de Sitter case, the future cosmological horizon. A horizon-regular flux formulation specifies the inner data and the distinct hyperboloidal and expanding asymptotic ends. Seventeen survey configurations are supplemented by a mean-flux scan at fixed four-geometry and paired flat/de Sitter comparisons down to $κM = 0.01$, where $K_0 = 3κ$. Varying the flux changes the preferred-foliation shear without changing the background seen by standard test matter. The paired local lapse and shear differences have effective powers close to two over the computed range, with the lapse comparison requiring a fixed time normalization. Continuous residuals, geometric reconstructions, and selected grid comparisons test the numerical solutions. An exact lapse bound excludes zeros in the regular stationary exterior block with $Δ_r > 0$. We distinguish singular finite-proper-distance endpoints from asymptotic trumpet ends and give conditional bounds on a stationary spacelike inner limit. A local cosmological interpretation requires additional matching assumptions; dynamical selection and the rotating interior endpoint are not determined by the stationary construction.

papers.title: Wireless AI Networks: Co-Adapting Communication Resources and Distributed Intelligence
papers.abstract: Distributed artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on wireless networks, where communication and computing resources shape how AI tasks are configured and executed. However, resource availability alone does not determine how effectively these tasks can be supported, since different information selections and transmission strategies may yield different AI performance under the same resource constraints. To address this challenge, this article presents Wireless AI Networks as a unified design perspective for bidirectional adaptation between wireless communication and distributed intelligence. Specifically, an AI-executable resource budget characterizes candidate AI configurations, while task-level information value guides their selection and wireless resource allocation. Building on these principles, a wireless-AI co-adaptation framework coordinates resource abstraction, joint configuration and allocation, and execution feedback. Two complementary experiments illustrate this perspective: update selection and statistical correction improve federated learning under identical model-update payload budgets, while sensitivity-aware power allocation reduces model accuracy degradation under the same average transmit-power constraint. Together, these results highlight the importance of coordinating resource feasibility and task-level information value in distributed AI execution.

papers.title: A Cheeger-Müller Theorem For Flat Superconnections
papers.abstract: For a flat superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on a ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-graded vector bundle $E$ over a closed oriented odd-dimensional manifold $M$, we prove a Cheeger-Müller type theorem as proposed by Arias Abad and Schätz. Namely, that the topological Reidemeister norm of ${\mathbb{A}}$ as defined by them equals the Ray-Singer metric defined by Mathai and Wu. The main step proves an analytic reduction result identified by Arias Abad and Schätz and formulated as a conjecture by the author, that the Ray-Singer metric coincides with that of the fibrewise cohomology $H(E,\partial)$ with its Gauss-Manin connection, where $\partial$ is the component of ${\mathbb{A}}$ of form degree zero, under the Knudsen-Mumford isomorphism associated to the form-degree spectral sequence. As an application, we consider Goette's Morse flat superconnection of a fibrewise Morse function on a fibre bundle with even-dimensional fibres over an oriented odd-dimensional base.

papers.title: Frustrated Magnetism from Dimerized $S = 1/2$ Co$^{2+}$ in Rose-Phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$
papers.abstract: We report the growth of high-quality single crystals and the magnetic, thermodynamic, and dielectric properties of rose-phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$, a low-symmetry magnet in which corner-sharing Co$^{2+}$ dimers form an approximately triangular network. Magnetic measurements reveal dominant antiferromagnetic interactions and pronounced anisotropy among effective $S=1/2$ Co$^{2+}$ moments. Broad low-temperature maxima in the magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity suggest the development of short-range magnetic correlations below approximately 4 K. The large separation between the absolute Curie--Weiss temperatures and the characteristic correlation temperature indicates strong magnetic frustration arising from competing interactions within the coupled-dimer network. Applied magnetic fields suppress these anomalies and reduce the recovered magnetic entropy, suggesting further enhancement of frustration under field. A systematic magnetodielectric response closely follows the field dependence of the magnetization, indicating coupling between magnetic and dielectric degrees of freedom. The low lattice symmetry enables multiple inequivalent exchange pathways and anisotropic interactions while relaxing symmetry constraints on coupling among spin, lattice, and dielectric degrees of freedom. These results establish rose-phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$ as a platform for exploring frustrated quantum magnetism and coupled functionalities in effective $S=1/2$ magnets.

papers.title: ARMOR: Adaptive Curriculum Meta-Learning for Noise-Robust RAG Reasoning
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in mitigating hallucinations by incorporating external knowledge. However, the retrieval process inevitably introduces noise, posing significant challenges to RAG robustness. Fundamentally, noise robustness is a composite competency encompassing noise identification, retrieval filtering, and robust reasoning. Unfortunately, existing methods often fail to capture this holistic nature, typically restricted to single-dimensional enhancements or hampered by noise-induced optimization interference. To address these limitations, we decompose RAG robustness into three sub-tasks: knowledge boundary perception, retrieval verification, and robust reasoning. Accordingly, we propose ARMOR, an Adaptive Curriculum Meta-Learning for Noise Robust RAG Reasoning. Inspired by the teaching process, ARMOR introduces an adaptive task scheduler as a teacher to curate training plans according to the absolute learning progress of RAG generators (Student). Distinct from GRPO, ARMOR utilizes inter-group advantage estimation during learning to effectively mitigate mode collapse caused by limited output spaces. Experiments on three complex reasoning datasets (2WikiMultiHopQA, MusiQue, and HotPotQA) indicate that ARMOR achieves synergistic improvements in retrieval noise robustness, significantly outperforming baselines in output quality.

papers.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Global structure-from-motion (SfM) commonly refines relative poses on individual image pairs and then estimates global rotations by rotation averaging. Pairwise refinement does not explicitly combine feature-level constraints with multi-view consistency during rotation initialization. We introduce Global Rotations from Aggregated Matches (GRAM), which estimates global rotations directly from initial relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals. GRAM replaces two-view relative-pose optimization and rotation averaging with a single stage. We further extend rotation- only imaging geometry to multiple views and develop Multi-view Optimization with Rotation-only Reprojection Error (MORE) for nonlinear global rotation refinement. Analytical Rotation-guided Translation (ART) derives locally scaled triplet translations from Linear Global Translation (LiGT) constraints and recovers global translations using weighted least squares. Synthetic and real-world experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: A level-set method for shape and topology optimization of Stokes--Darcy flows with Beavers--Joseph--Saffman coupling
papers.abstract: We propose a level-set method for shape and topology optimization of Stokes--Darcy flows with Beavers--Joseph--Saffman interface coupling. We formulate the Stokes--Darcy system with BJS interface conditions using a level-set representation and establish existence and uniqueness of its solution. We further prove existence of minimizers for the viscous-energy minimization and least-squares inverse problems within this framework. Continuous Fréchet differentiability of the control-to-state map is proved, and objective derivatives are derived using an adjoint approach. A reaction--diffusion evolution scheme combined with mixed finite elements is developed to find the optimized interface and accommodate topology changes. Two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments verify the derived sensitivities and demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in minimizing viscous energy dissipation and reconstructing interfaces from partial and noisy velocity observations.

papers.title: Super-resolution quantum imaging via multiphoton correlation
papers.abstract: The resolution of conventional imaging is fundamentally constrained by the diffraction limit. Here we demonstrate that this limit can be overcome using classical thermal light, through the correlation of multiphoton subsystems. By resolving the photon numbers detected in the two arms of a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer, the correlation function exhibits a narrowed peak or dip whose width is tunable via the average photon number. Temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively, are experimentally achieved. As a proof-of-principle experiment, a double-pinhole that is completely unresolved by standard ghost imaging becomes clearly distinguishable via the correlation of two-photon versus zero-photon. The principle of this super-resolution imaging can be interpreted as a combination of classical super-resolution imaging and quantum super-resolution imaging. This work provides a versatile platform for super-resolution imaging and lithography, and opens a new avenue for exploring the boundary between classical and nonclassical phenomena.

papers.title: Nonassociative gradings on infinite-dimensional triangular algebras
papers.abstract: We study group gradings on triangular algebras relative to a well-ordered basis, with multiplication $x\circ_λy=xy+λyx$. For $λ\notin\{0,\pm1\}$, every grading on a finite-dimensional triangular algebra is isomorphic to an elementary grading. In infinite dimension, the same conclusion holds for the algebra of finite-range maps, for the finite-map algebra on a basis of order type $ω$, and for closed gradings on the full triangular algebra. The infinite-dimensional results also hold for $λ=1$ in characteristic different from $2$. For intermediate algebras whose finite-range ideal is graded, we obtain an elementary description relative to a unitriangular basis. The proofs construct neutral associative idempotents with singleton diagonal supports. We also prove that the radical of the full triangular algebra is graded for every nonzero $λ$, and that gradings on the finite-range algebra and closed gradings on the full algebra have finite support under the classification hypotheses.

papers.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
papers.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

papers.title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Iodine-vacancy migration and association are important factors in the structural stability of halide perovskites. Although neighboring vacancies have been suggested to form energetically favorable pairs, their stability and reconfiguration under finite-temperature lattice deformation remain unclear. Here, we combine machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain. The MLMD trajectories reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of short-time hopping fractions on strain, with strong isotropic compression favoring point-like separation and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping. Notably, biaxial compression produces distinct orientation-dependent responses: vacancy pairs initially aligned with the compressed plane preferentially undergo separation, whereas those perpendicular to the plane predominantly exhibit relay hopping. Complementary static calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential yield repulsive interactions for all configurations examined. These findings highlight the importance of finite-temperature dynamics and strain-dependent local geometry in understanding vacancy-pair stability and reconfiguration in halide perovskites.

papers.title: An asymptotic preserving scheme for kinetic equations describing bacterial traveling pulses
papers.abstract: We consider a kinetic model for bacterial chemotaxis that describes the propagation of traveling pulses driven by a nutrient and a self-produced chemoattractant. In the diffusive regime, the model converges to a macroscopic drift-diffusion system with bounded chemotactic fluxes. We construct a fully discrete asymptotic preserving (AP) finite difference scheme based on a micro-macro decomposition of the kinetic equation. The method is stable uniformly with respect to the scaling parameter and, as this parameter tends to zero, reduces to a consistent discretization of the limiting macroscopic equations. We prove positivity and mass conservation for the limiting scheme, and use a positivity-preserving correction for the kinetic solver. Numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed traveling pulses at both the kinetic and the macroscopic level, validate the theoretical traveling wave speed, and illustrate the convergence of the kinetic model to its macroscopic limit.

papers.title: LangDepth: Vision-Language Scene Priors for Semantic Binning and Cross-Domain Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.abstract: Monocular depth estimation has advanced through large-scale pretraining and strong visual backbones, yet metric depth remains sensitive to scene-level scale. Indoor rooms and outdoor driving scenes occupy very different depth ranges, but most depth decoders infer this global structure implicitly from visual features. We ask whether scene-level semantic structure can instead act as an upstream prior that shapes the metric output space before dense prediction. We present LangDepth (SemanticBins), a monocular depth architecture that couples strong visual features with a scene-conditioned output space. A frozen CLIP encoder and a learnable bank of scene- and geometry-oriented concept keys convert image features into a compact scene descriptor, without requiring per-image text or an external captioner. A Scene Prior Module (SPM) maps this descriptor to a scene-conditioned metric depth interval, providing a global range anchor before dense decoding. In parallel, a DINOv2-L backbone with a lightweight FPN extracts dense visual features, and a Per-Pixel Assignment Network (PPAN) assigns pixels to the scene-prescribed bin structure. A confidence gate fuses the dense visual estimate with the SPM prior. We train LangDepth jointly on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI under a modest supervised depth budget, without web-scale depth supervision or pseudo-labelled depth data. A single model achieves delta_1 = 0.960 on NYU, 0.960 on KITTI, 0.887 on DIODE indoor, 0.946 on iBims-1, and 0.861 on SUN RGB-D. Beyond aggregate accuracy, the SPM predicts compact indoor ranges and much wider outdoor KITTI ranges, the gate becomes SPM-dominant on outdoor scenes, and perturbing the routed scene context causes large drops on KITTI and iBims-1. These results support scene-conditioned output spaces as a practical and interpretable mechanism for cross-domain monocular depth estimation.

papers.title: Optimal Radial Weighting for Robust Mutual Fund Selection
papers.abstract: Identifying skilled mutual funds requires methods that distinguish positive alphas from sampling variation when many funds are evaluated simultaneously. Heavy-tailed returns and dependence across funds complicate this task. We propose a robust selection procedure based on radially weighted alpha estimation in linear factor pricing models. The method uses both the directions and lengths of standardized residuals, estimates marginal scales from pairwise residual differences, and accounts for the estimation of factor loadings. Within the proposed class, inverse-norm weighting minimizes the asymptotic variance of the alpha estimators and maximizes the local asymptotic power of individual tests at a common significance level. For radial weights fixed conditional on the factor design, we establish asymptotic false discovery rate control under elliptically symmetric errors and show that the proportion of sufficiently strong positive-alpha funds selected tends to one. The theory accommodates comparable cross-sectional and time-series dimensions and nonvanishing alphas. We also develop a smoothed implementation and assess its finite-sample properties. Simulations show higher true discovery proportions than least-squares and spatial-sign methods under heavy-tailed distributions and improved numerical stability from smoothing. An application to U.S. equity mutual funds examines the subsequent performance of portfolios formed from the selected funds.

papers.title: BridgeKV: Large-Model Prefill and Small-Model Decoding for LLM Inference via KV Cache Translation
papers.abstract: LLM inference has two phases with different bottlenecks: LLM prefill runs once per request and is compute-intensive. Decoding repeats for every output token and is limited by memory bandwidth. To address the challenges associated with this issue, different solutions have been proposed. All of these solutions use the same model for both prefill and decode phases. We propose BridgeKV, which uses a larger model for prefill and a smaller model of the same family for decoding. A lightweight KV-stitching module translates the larger model's prompt cache into the smaller model's cache layout. It handles differences in cache shape and representation through learned local layer mixing and separate nonlinear maps for keys and values. With both models frozen, we train the module to align their caches and make the smaller model follow the larger model's next-token predictions. A second training stage adds low-rank adapters when further task adaptation is needed. Across six model pairs and five datasets, BridgeKV outperforms fine-tuned small-model baselines with matched trainable parameter budgets in all 30 settings. It closes up to 80% of the quality gap to using the larger model for both phases. On one A40 GPU, Llama-3.1-Instruct-8B to Llama-3.2-Instruct-1B achieves 3.0X faster requests than the larger model alone, with latency close to the smaller model alone. BridgeKV can improve the hardware and system solutions that separate prefill and decode phases across GPUs. A separate serving simulation models request arrivals, queues, and cache transfer. For Llama-3.1-Instruct-70B to Llama-3.2-Instruct-1B, it predicts up to 33.86X faster requests and 27.5X lower energy use than using the larger model for both prefill and decode phases.

papers.title: Proof of the Rényi QNEC
papers.abstract: We give a general proof of the Rényi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.

papers.title: An optimal quantum strategy for the $2$-hat game
papers.abstract: We study the two-player hat game as a two-input, three-output non-local game. We calculate the quantum commuting value and show that it coincides with the quantum one. In particular, we show that \[ω_{\rm q}(H_2)=ω_{\mathrm{qc}}(H_2)=\frac{15+\sqrt{33}}{36}\approx 0.576238.\] We achieve the optimal quantum advantage using a shared non-maximally entangled qutrit state. To establish optimality, we exploit the game's symmetry under the dihedral group $D_8$ and apply its representation theory to substantially reduce the complexity of the underlying matrix problem. We also determine the no-signalling value $ω_{\mathrm{ns}}(H_2)=2/3$.

papers.title: Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps
papers.abstract: Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. For every countable set $P\subset[0,1]$, we prove that the set of points whose orbit closure is disjoint from $P$ is absolute winning on $[0,1]$. Our proof combines a potential game argument with an interval tree constructed from successive returns.

papers.title: Calibrated Alarm Thresholds for Compact Fire and Smoke Detectors
papers.abstract: Compact object detectors such as YOLOv8n are a common choice for camera-based fire and smoke detection on low-power devices. These detectors are usually evaluated with box-level metrics such as mean average precision, and their outputs are turned into decisions with a fixed confidence threshold such as 0.25 or 0.5. A fire monitoring system, however, makes one decision per image: raise an alarm or not. In this paper we evaluate two publicly available compact detectors on the D-Fire test set at the image level. We compare three simple rules for turning box detections into one alarm score per image, and we use a split conformal procedure to choose the alarm threshold from held-out images so that the expected fraction of missed fire and smoke images stays below a chosen target. We find that the same fixed threshold leads to very different miss rates for the two detectors, 17.3 and 8.4 percent at a threshold of 0.5, while the calibrated threshold meets miss-rate targets of 10, 5 and 1 percent for both detectors and all three rules. At a 5 percent target, the false alarm rate on images without fire or smoke stays between 1.2 and 3.0 percent. We also find that smoke-only images stay below the target even when the overall target is met, and we describe the main failure cases.

papers.title: Causal Resolution of Undefined Answers in Datalog with Negation
papers.abstract: Unstratified negation may leave the answer to a Boolean Datalog query undefined under the well-founded semantics. We study database causality in this setting by asking which fact insertions and deletions realize a prescribed transition and which other changes preserve the observed query answer while making a designated fact pivotal. Such a set of changes to other facts is a contingency for the designated fact and the prescribed transition. Our game representation assigns one shared move to each mutable fact and preserves query values and intervention distances. Pairing source and target certificates characterizes all minimum contingencies for the six transitions among true, false, and undefined. When inserting or deleting a move resolves a draw, a directed tree traces the newly winning and losing positions along alternating paths to the source of that move. For the fixed one-rule win--move program, deciding whether a contingency of size at most $k$ exists is $\mathrm{NP}$-complete for each transition, even on bounded-degree graphs. Computing the minimum size is $\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}[\log]}$-complete, and counting minimum contingencies is $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. When only one of true and false is reachable, the prime implicants of undefinedness satisfied at the observation cover every undefined state, and their supports induce nonempty subtrees of a common tree, we compute a minimum resolving intervention in polynomial time from the game instance. From the explicit tree and these implicants, we construct an equally large family of disjoint supports, certifying optimality.

papers.title: Graph-Sparse Distributed Predictive Control for Multi-Robot Motion Planning vianEdge-Consensus ADMM
papers.abstract: This paper presents a distributed model predictive control (MPC) architecture for collision-avoiding motion planning of planar robots with double-integrator dynamics. To reduce coordination demands, a time-varying predicted conflict graph selects relevant pairwise interactions. The associated collision-avoidance constraints are convexified once per MPC update using warm-start trajectories, yielding a fixed convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting QP is then decomposed using an edge-consensus formulation of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), enabling parallel robot-local optimization and independent closed-form projections onto separating half-spaces. Execution is selectively supervised by a centralized high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) QP when the distributed candidate does not satisfy the direct-execution conditions. Evaluated in C++ simulations involving 8, 16, and 32 robots, the proposed architecture achieves collision-free execution and substantially improves computational scalability while maintaining task-level performance comparable to a centralized complete-graph baseline.

papers.title: Advantage Distillation in Paired-State Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: We investigate advantage distillation for paired-state Loop-Back quantum key distribution, with a fixed optical station serving a lightweight portable terminal. Alice prepares two polarization-encoded pulses, Bob selects and applies a polarization filter to each pulse, and Alice infers his selections from the returned detection pattern. The proposed advantage-distillation step selects consistent blocks of three two-bit records using two independent public parity checks on a minimal connected graph. The closing edge of a parity polygon is shown to be redundant: any spanning tree of the same vertices has the same acceptance set. We derive exact acceptance probabilities, residual-error laws, and retention rates. Under independent bit errors, the three-record filter reduces the leading error term from e to e^2, while its cost in discarded records and public information is accounted for explicitly. A modular security theorem bounds the additional guessing advantage available to an adversary after syndrome disclosure and block acceptance, including arbitrary quantum side information. We also evaluate a specified single-photon passive-tap optical channel, obtaining a positive conditional entropy bound and exact accepted-block security quantities. This parity-based advantage-distillation step detects discrepancies by postselection; it does not correct individual errors and is intended to precede conventional reconciliation. The architecture suggests two further directions: hybrid filtering and reconciliation, and key establishment between portable users accessing a shared quantum station.

papers.title: SpinSCI: Mask-Conditioned Spatial-Temporal Spin Transformer for Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging
papers.abstract: Video snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) recovers multiple frames from one spatiotemporally coded measurement. This paper proposes SpinSCI, a mask-conditioned Spatial-Temporal Spin Transformer whose Mask-Conditioned Ising Refinement Block (MC-IRB) combines attention logits and sensing information to form signed spin couplings. Finite mean-field updates gate residual feature refinement. Physics-guided initialization and final data consistency incorporate the measurement model. Compared with HiSViT$_9$, SpinSCI achieves average PSNR gains of 0.51 dB, 0.23 dB, and 0.04 dB on small-scale gray, mid-scale color, and large-scale color benchmarks, respectively, with 16.9% fewer parameters, 21.0-21.6% fewer FLOPs, 17.1-49.9% lower latency, and 62.3-63.3% lower peak memory. Relative to DU-9stg, average PSNR differs by at most 0.13 dB across these benchmarks, with 28.2-28.7% fewer FLOPs, 64.6-71.7% lower inference latency, and 30.1-35.0% lower peak memory. Qualitative comparisons on the real benchmark further show recovery of fine details and textures. Code and reference checkpoints are available at https://github.com/skethz/SpinSCI.

papers.title: Spectral Rank and Step-Direction Dynamics in Language-Model Post-Training
papers.abstract: Language-model post-training modifies weights through cumulative updates and successive displacements, yet existing studies report seemingly conflicting spectral properties: nearly full-rank updates and low stable-rank changes. We show these observations are compatible and characterize update directions during training. For singular values following $σ_i \propto i^{-α}$ with $0 < α\leq 1/2$, we prove that stable rank becomes negligible relative to fixed-energy rank as dimension increases. Full singular value decompositions of selected OLMo-2-7B updates confirm this separation: three proximal policy optimization (PPO) attention updates have stable ranks of 9.6-18.3 but require 532-1,222 singular components to capture 80% of their energy. We next compute consecutive checkpoint-displacement cosines from full-model inner products. Across nine publicly released reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) stages, all 131 adjacent pairs have negative cosines on their native checkpoint grids, including PPO and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning comparisons across four model families show configuration-dependent alignment, including negative late-training cosines for Mistral and FP32 Llama. Finally, a controlled OLMo-2-1B study with three paired seeds and a 2,048-token response cap compares group-relative advantages against a learned critic with generalized advantage estimation (GAE). At matched 60-rollout windows, late-training mean cosines are +0.259 and +0.012, respectively; the paired critic-minus-group difference is -0.247 (seed-level 95% interval [-0.358, -0.137]). These findings distinguish spectral concentration, energy coverage, and trajectory direction, and demonstrate that the advantage system influences directional alignment under matched training conditions.

papers.title: GeoPilot: Diagnosis-Guided Interventions and Geometric Evaluation for Aerial Reconstruction
papers.abstract: When a mesh reconstructed from aerial remote-sensing imagery disagrees with reference geometry, deciding what to change requires a diagnosis of the reconstruction process. We present GeoPilot, a workflow that turns diagnostics and prior observations into executable program or camera-configuration interventions. A large language model proposes the change, numerical tools reconstruct the mesh, and an external evaluator measures its geometry under a stated coordinate and reference protocol. The main case tests a shared-intrinsics hypothesis proposed before the comparison. On 224 Metashape-raster development images, shared intrinsics improved all six native-coordinate measures and reduced mean surface-to-reference distance by 7.04%. Reference-assisted alignment fitted and evaluated on separate within-scene checkerboard samples reversed the mean-distance ranking, limiting that gain to native-frame delivery. A separate matched comparison on publisher-undistorted images favored fixed published cameras on all six measures, reducing mean distance by 12.11%; the cameras retain upstream image and laser-scanning adjustment information. With one reconstruction per configuration, these comparisons provide conditional evidence for camera handling. Three end-to-end runs each delivered a mesh and six-metric evaluation from all 327 images of a second development scene.

papers.title: Becker's Conjecture on Compositions of Higher Degree Diagonal Forms
papers.abstract: Becker's conjecture asserts that a rational composition of sums of $d$-th powers of size $[r,s,n]$, with $d>2$, requires $n \ge rs$. We show that this formulation fails over every characteristic-zero field in odd degree, and in every degree over a suitable finite extension of $\Q$. Over formally real fields in even degree, however, we prove that every polynomial composition satisfies $n\ge rs$.

papers.title: Origin of Tensor Polarized Structure of the Deuteron
papers.abstract: The microscopic origin of the deuteron tensor polarized structure function $b_1$ remains unresolved. Conventional nuclear models attribute a nonzero $b_1$ mainly to the $D$-wave component of the deuteron wave function, but generally fail to reproduce the magnitude and momentum-dependence observed by the HERMES experiment. Using a QCD-based light-front framework with degrees of freedom beyond the conventional nucleonic picture, in particular including hidden-color components and relativistic spin--momentum correlations, we find that a small but nonzero estimated hidden-color admixture can be sufficient to generate a substantial tensor response ($b_1(x)$), while it is essentially insensitive to the $D$-wave component. The physical $D$-wave probability of $0.85\%$, fixed by the empirical quadrupole moment, changes $b_1$ by only $1.7\%$, with the dominant contribution arising from the colored-cluster $S$-wave sector. These results demonstrate that the tensor-polarized structure of the deuteron is driven primarily by hidden-color dynamics rather than by the $D$-wave component.

papers.title: Model-family selection and recovery-gate design in generator-based noise tomography
papers.abstract: Family selection in generator-model noise tomography, usually quoted as a property of the hardware, is a hypothesis test whose shot floor is closed form, $N^{*}=λ_{\mathrm{req}}/(r_{\mathrm{b}} S)^{2}$, controlled by the absolute bias $r_{\mathrm{b}} S$ rather than by the relative residual $r_{\mathrm{b}}$, and therefore computable for any device before a single shot is taken. The same computation prices the recovery gates, because the fingerprint that fixes a family's residual and the Fisher information that ranks the designs are read off the same map: there is no design-independent verdict and no family-independent design optimum. Whether a design can move that price is structural, not numerical: a bias confined to the block every design measures identically is design-blind, while one that reaches the code blocks can be repriced by a factor of sixty-eight. The two platforms here are its extremes, at $98.1\%$ and $48.0\%$ in the design-blind block. At the reference point the floor is $1.1\times10^{7}$ and $6.7\times10^{6}$ shots per component for the two families, so at the $10^{5}$ shots a run spends the test has power $0.053$ at a level of $0.05$ and the residual it reports is shot noise. Rebuilding the fingerprint under each of the sixty-four designs moves the floor by $68$ on one platform and $1.7$ on the other, and the most precise design costs ten times more shots for the verdict than the cheapest to test. All sixty-four placements are full rank, so the design problem is one of conditioning: at three gates the rms varies by factors of $2.7$ and $3.9$ with placement alone, while the optimum over counts is flat. At five qubits the same rule moves the floor by $21$, while the verdict itself costs $10^{9}$ shots; checked against the calibration of a real three-qubit register, the floor is a requirement on systematic control before it is a shot count.

papers.title: Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences
papers.abstract: In a frequency-hopping (FH) system, to reduce interference to the received signal, each user's frequency hopping sequence (FHS) shall have wide-gap property. In this paper, we update the upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS) with parameters $(v,s,λ;e)$ where $v=ks, k\ge 3, λ=k$ and $s\ge k(k-1)+1$ is odd. We completely prove the existence of such WGFHSs for $k\le 3$.

papers.title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.

papers.title: Reproducible quantum clustering for single-cell transcriptome atlases
papers.abstract: Current single-cell clustering pipelines discard most genes and can yield inconsistent clusters across random seeds. We introduce KQE-2, a training-free hybrid quantum-classical framework for reproducible whole-transcriptome clustering. KQE-2 maps cells into entanglement-free quantum states, enabling exact feature evaluation on classical hardware and direct checks on a quantum processor. Theoretically, we prove that removing entanglement is necessary and sufficient to bound single-qubit feature variance locally. Practically, while retraining scVI shifted 14% of cells and altered rare-type markers and drug targets, KQE-2 delivered identical biology across runs. On standard highly variable genes, the quantum encoding alone raised accuracy on a developing cortex from 0.61 to 0.79. KQE-2 scales to 11.4 million nuclei on one server, outperforming the compared methods on eight of ten complete atlases (and within the best method's run-to-run range on two), and leads on six even under standard downstream clustering.

papers.title: Breaking the $\sqrt{d}$ Communication Barrier in Federated Sampling with Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: This work proposes the Adaptive Federated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (AFHMC) for Bayesian federated learning (FL) tasks. The prior work on HMC applications for FL achieves $O(\sqrt{d}/ε)$ communication cost under log-convex distributions, already demonstrating its advantage over the Langevin dynamic-based counterpart. Based on a refined analysis, this paper further reveals the benefit of HMC for the FL regime by incorporating a control mechanism for local node shifts. We prove that AFHMC at most requires $O(\{d/ε^2\}^{1/3})$ communication cost up to a logarithmic term, which is significantly better than the existing results. Moreover, the proposed method adapts to client heterogeneity. Under low-heterogeneity settings (i.e., the target sampling precision $ε^2$ is higher than the heterogeneity level), the communication rate of AFHMC can be as good as $O(\log(d/ε^2))$, resembling the communication costs for FL optimization tools. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first logarithmic communication complexity result for federated sampling, even though it requires low heterogeneity. Numerically, we also justify AFHMC's advantage under the low-heterogeneity regime. Our code is available at https://github.com/laaaarrywang/Adaptive-Federated-HMC

papers.title: A Review of Measurement System Uncertainty Handoffs Across the Manufacturing Decision Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Measurement systems generate uncertain information that downstream manufacturing decisions often consume as if fixed. This structured integrative review examines how measurement error, uncertainty, GR\&R estimates, calibration evidence, and drift information are handed off into capability inference, retrospective Phase I reference estimation, prospective Phase II monitoring, operational action, and requalification. Studies are compared by the upstream uncertain object, whether it is known, calibrated, or estimated, its propagation mechanism, the downstream decision, and the validation boundary. The synthesis distinguishes recorded production data from latent-process targets: measurement-system information calibrates limits, uncertainty statements, replication, guard bands, or losses, but does not reveal the realized random error in an individual record. Within the retained literature, measurement-to-capability and measurement-to-monitoring mechanisms are more extensively represented by model-based studies, whereas prospective evidence is thinner where statistical results must support source attribution, cost-sensitive action, and requalification. A decision-handoff spine separates measurement generation, statistical inference, and operational validation so that capability, stability, attribution, and intervention effectiveness are not conflated. The review is integrative rather than exhaustive. Its contribution is an auditable measurement-science framework that preserves provenance, information status, validity conditions, and downstream use while identifying claims that are model-supported, conditionally calibrated, or not yet operationally validated.

papers.title: The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem
papers.abstract: We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. In the positive-definite case, we determine the representing measures, prove their uniqueness and specify the admissible endpoint masses. No boundedness assumption on the support or asymptotic conditions on the recurrence coefficients are imposed.

papers.title: Silinx: An Open, Browser-Based HDL Design Platform for Teaching Digital Systems on FPGA Boards
papers.abstract: Many digital systems courses teach on FPGA boards whose vendor tool is no longer maintained: the Digilent Basys2 and Nexys2 (Xilinx Spartan-3E) and Nexys3 and Atlys (Spartan-6) need Xilinx ISE 14.7, discontinued since 2013 and hard to install on the computers and tablets students use today. The author presents Silinx, a free (AGPL-3.0) HDL design platform for teaching that keeps ISE's Project Navigator workflow but runs in a web browser with nothing to install. A module can be written in VHDL or Verilog, in C or C++ through Silinx HLS, which is compatible with AMD's Vitis HLS and passes all 73 of its introductory examples, or drawn as a schematic, an ASM chart, a state diagram, a Boolean function with its Karnaugh map, or a Petri net, from which its HDL is generated. Designs are checked with explanations written for beginners, simulated, run on an emulated board, built, and programmed onto a real board over WebUSB. The implementation flow is open and runs in the browser: Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, with Silinx's own device data, timing model and bitstream writer for the Spartan-3E and Spartan-6, built by black-box observation of ISE's documented tools; Lattice iCE40 boards use the existing open iCE40 tools, and further families are planned. ISE is the oracle: Silinx's bitstreams are byte-identical to those ISE writes for the same placed and routed design, and pass ISE's design rule check. Against ISE at the same optimization goal, the open flow uses 15% fewer slices with 14% shorter critical paths when optimizing for area, and 21% fewer slices with 8% shorter critical paths when optimizing for speed (geometric means over 45 open-source designs built by both flows). The author also describes how the platform was developed with AI coding agents under test-first project rules.

papers.title: Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox
papers.abstract: Many of the most consequential advances promised by AI, from curing diseases and inventing new technologies to formulating new scientific theories, are fundamentally creative acts. Yet creativity is uniquely difficult to learn because it faces a creative paradox: learning to repeat past examples of creative success makes those specific examples more likely to recur, inhibiting the very creativity desired. This work argues that creativity is better modeled as an explicit process rather than as a property of individual artifacts, and proposes to learn the underlying generative principles behind the creative process. In particular, to escape the paradox, we introduce creative priming (CP), wherein a trained priming model generates a prompt-specific primer that assists a response model in being creative, explicitly decoupling the creative process from response generation. The priming model learns through GRPO, rewarding primers that lead to responses that are novel, high-quality, and diverse, thereby reinforcing the process that yields creative responses without reinforcing any specific response.

papers.title: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving
papers.abstract: Lazy container-image pulling makes cold starts of autoscaled model-serving fleets on Kubernetes nearly independent of model size, but it moves the model's bytes into a node-level cache that the platform neither bounds nor accounts for. This article establishes, by experiment, two impossibility results for that cache. A monitoring-side remedy cannot catch its failure: a sentinel readiness probe stays green while 272 of 280 files are unreadable. A platform-side remedy cannot contain it: kubelet, given full disk-pressure visibility, frees 0 bytes and evicts 26 bystander pods, because its reclamation actuator is keyed to an accounting that does not know the cache exists. The article then eliminates the failure class inside the component that owns the bytes, with no change to kubelet or the container runtime interface, by two design rules: a byte budget whose pressure signal is keyed to filesystem truth, so that a never-blocking, lossy accounting still enforces a hard bound (held against about 301,000 dropped updates), and pass-through semantics under which a failed cache write never becomes a failed read, with the coupling traced to a single io.MultiWriter. Across six pre-specified campaigns on AWS, upstream stargz-snapshotter fails 273 of 280 model files at 90% cache pre-fill; the proposed system reads all 150.3 GB with zero errors at +18.5% completion cost and holds the budget under a live read, co-tenancy, and a three-node fleet. A source audit shows the missing bound generalizes to SOCI and Nydus. The implementation is open source and has been proposed upstream.

papers.title: Dense Flow from Adaptive Correspondence
papers.abstract: Optical flow requires reliable matching from sufficient visual context and precise motion at every pixel. Existing methods such as WAFT match and estimate flow on the same coarse grids, then recover dense flow through learned upsampling, without explicitly linking visual support for matching to dense flow reconstruction. Our key insight is that dense pixel-level flow does not require equally dense matching. We decouple correspondence scale from flow resolution by adapting the size and shape of spatial supports to image structure for reliable matching, while reusing these supports for precise dense flow reconstruction. We realize this in Flow from Adaptive Token Estimation (FATE), whose token supports expand within coherent regions and contract near motion boundaries. Shared pixel-to-token associations pool features for matching and reconstruct pixel flow from token motions. Flow supervision jointly trains pixel grouping, token matching, and flow estimation without grouping labels, allowing FATE to anticipate which pixels are likely to move together from appearance alone. Trained on FlyingChairs/FlyingThings3D, FATE achieves the highest zero-shot accuracy on Sintel Final and KITTI, a critical setting given scarce real-world flow labels. For visible pixels, FATE improves accuracy within coherent regions, and more near motion boundaries. Its largest gains occur where direct matches are unavailable: Occluded or out-of-frame pixels account for roughly 10% of valid pixels but 50% of WAFT's total error. Experiments show that adaptive correspondence through pixel-to-token grouping enables reliable matching and precise pixel-level flow, improving generalization to unseen real scenes.

papers.title: Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{ψ,φ}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{ψ,φ}$ and that of the composition operator $C_φ$.

papers.title: The Alt-Phillips Multiple Membrane Free Boundary Problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by diffusion--reaction processes in porous catalysts, we study an Alt--Phillips model for ordered membranes with weighted gap interactions. The model connects adhesive harmonic junctions \cite{DSS24} and forced multiple membranes \cite{SY19} through the exponent $0<γ<1$. For arbitrary positive weights, we prove optimal $C^{1,β-1}$ regularity, where $β=2/(2-γ)$, and obtain nontrivial $β$-homogeneous blowup limits through Weiss almost monotonicity. Under strict discrete concavity of the weights, we establish a gluing principle, minimality of flat single-gap cones, and $C^{1,α}$ free boundary regularity at points admitting such blowups. We also classify all one-dimensional vertically critical cones. For three membranes, we identify cone families that are non-minimizing for small $γ$ and minimizing near $γ=1$.

papers.title: Correctness Metric Matters: NWD-Based Calibration Loss for Tiny Person Detection in UAV Infrared Imagery
papers.abstract: Detection calibration aligns predicted confidence with empirical correctness. Existing calibration losses inherit their correctness definition from box regression, specifically IoU against a hard threshold. We show that this target is geometrically ill-posed for tiny objects in UAV infrared imagery, where persons occupy less than 0.1\% of the image. The same pixel error is penalized more heavily as the target shrinks, so binary prediction calibration (BPC) actively suppresses confidences that should be high. On HIT-UAV, BPC with an IoU target degrades image-level localization-aware ECE (LaECE) from 0.0689 to 0.0761, 0.0649 to 0.0733, and 0.0653 to 0.0682 across Low, Mid, and High signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) groups. We replace the IoU target with a continuous, scale-invariant normalized Wasserstein distance (NWD). The NWD target reduces LaECE\(_{\mathrm{NWD}}\) relative to BPC+IoU on all three groups (\(p<10^{-7}\)) with mAP neutral (0.9356 vs.\ 0.9347), and an independent center-offset anchor confirms that the gain is a genuine geometric correction. The improvement holds across a broad plateau of calibration weights. The NWD formulation requires no inference-time mapping layer. If a validation-fitted isotonic map is applied on top of it, calibration is lowered further, and the two corrections act on different components of the same error. The metric-level remedy has a measurable boundary. Target-background thermal pairing in the training distribution and detection-level aggregation under per-image detection-count heterogeneity lie outside it. Both are quantified independently of the NWD target.

papers.title: A Bifurcation-Theoretic Framework for the Controllability of Emergent Intelligent Systems
papers.abstract: Real-world intelligent systems must reconcile two demands: the adaptability conferred by emergence and the steerability required for accountable deployment. We show that these demands are governed by two distinct bifurcations on the same object and that, consequently, increased capability does not imply increased controllability. Emergence is a bifurcation of the capability variable $S$, with criterion $Γ:=\mathcal F'(0)>1$ equivalent to the existence of a unique positive stable fixed point of a self-consistency equation, following solely from the concavity of $\mathcal F$. Controllability is a bifurcation of the permission variable $c$, whose dynamics include an erosion term and exhibit a saddle-node fold with hysteresis as the gate criterion $ρ^\ast$ crosses unity. Three quantitative results follow: the critical exponent distinguishes families rather than classifying the transition; the gating-cost bound $K(M)\propto\log(1+M)$ grows with scope, not capability; and the fold threshold is $γ_c\approx4μκ$. Calibrated in both directions, the criteria reproduce the two-dimensional Ising transition, admit two true-feedback order parameters, and reject nine candidate quantities, supporting the conclusion that the order parameter is geometric rather than capability-related. Since permission cannot be endogenized and no deployed system has been measured to satisfy $Γ>1$ and $ρ^\ast>1$ simultaneously, increased capability does not imply controllability.

papers.title: Can the Remaining Answers Change the Prediction? Worst-Case Stability Checks for Personalized Rating Models
papers.abstract: Missing ratings can overturn a personalized model's current prediction. For completed models with additive response scores, exact worst case bounds check all missing assignments without changing the current predictor. We evaluate this audit retrospectively in two self-triage cohorts, 108 clinicians rating three simulated psychiatric interviews, and 126 counseling demonstrations annotated by ten experts. Under shared random half histories, Fisher adaptation based on observed ratings reduces log loss relative to response frequency by 0.1071 nats in the clinician audit (95% CI [0.0867,0.1261]) and 0.0223 in counseling (95% CI[0.0121,0.0321]). The counseling test excludes target experts and source videos from training. Certification covers 5.4% and 10.5% of targets; fixed width acquisition raises coverage to 13.7% and 28.6% at the same budgets. With weights and responses held fixed, the observed-rating update also has lower loss than an affine partial update while certifying exactly the same evaluated targets. The certificate establishes agreement with the completed model, not correctness or stability at intermediate updates. These rating tasks test the method; clinical usefulness remains untested.

papers.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
papers.abstract: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. While particle filtering conventionally uses these weights only for state estimation, we also use them to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments in partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation demonstrate improvements in both state estimation and task performance compared to action generation without filtering, using the same pretrained model and no additional test-time information.

papers.title: The tertiary invariant and discrete Green-Schwarz couplings in heterotic string theory
papers.abstract: The tertiary invariant is a recently introduced pairing between two-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(0,1)$ supersymmetric quantum field theories, motivated by topological modular forms. We evaluate it directly from its definition for the sigma models on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ with unit $H$-flux, paired with the internal theories of the non-supersymmetric $\mathfrak{so}(16)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(16)$ heterotic string and of the near-horizon region of the non-supersymmetric heterotic 6-brane, respectively. Regarding the target spaces as $S^3$ bundles over spheres, we fill in every fiber with a four-disk carrying a gauge instanton and reduce the invariant to the index of a Dirac operator on the base. We find nonzero values of order three and two, which determine the Green-Schwarz couplings of the two theories on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, respectively. The former, a $\mathbb{Z}_{3}$-valued discrete topological term of the $\mathfrak{so}(16)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(16)$ theory, was previously studied through anomaly inflow to NS5-branes. Our computation, which uses only the worldsheet theories, agrees exactly with that result and thus confirms the anomaly inflow.

papers.title: Scarcity Pricing for State-of-Charge Management in Real-Time Markets Under Intra-Day Uncertainty
papers.abstract: The growth in renewable resources will increase net load variability and forecast error. Energy storage resources can provide flexibility when ramp capability is limited and contribute to load leveling over the day. The challenge for system operators is how to balance these two functions in real time, when updated net load forecasts are available for a limited lookahead horizon. U.S. electricity markets are seeking ways to manage state-of-charge (SoC) within their energy markets to more efficiently utilize these resources. We propose a method to manage energy storage SoC in a real-time market by extending Hogan's (2013) scarcity pricing framework. A day-ahead SoC schedule is modified using existing multi-interval real-time unit commitment engines as net load forecasts change. To address 30-minute-ahead forecast errors, an updated 5-minute SoC target and a dynamically updated shortage price for violating the constraint are provided to each economic dispatch. We simulate PJM's energy markets for 365 days and demonstrate reliability improvements relative to a strategy that enforces the day-ahead schedule. We show cost reductions and improved price formation relative to a strategy that updates target quantities but uses an administratively chosen shortage penalty.

papers.title: Wavelength-resolved polarization characterization of supercontinuum vector beams
papers.abstract: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry.
