Separating boundary occurrences from interior ones gives an $O(n\log n)$-word index that reports the $c$ answers in $O(\log n+c)$ time and supports counting and longest queries in $O(\log n)$ time. Our main result reduces reporting space to $O(n)$ words, with $O((c+1)\log^{1+\varepsilon} n)$ query time and $O(n\log^{1+\varepsilon} n)$ construction time for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Thus, after preprocessing, reporting requires no additive scan of the queried substring, which is particularly useful for long queries with few answers. Independently, we prove that at most $3(s-1)$ MCS occurrences of any length-$s$ substring cross a fixed gap between consecutive characters, with maximality evaluated inside that substring. The same bound holds for global MCSs contained in a length-$s$ block. A family over two letters attains $\lfloor(s-1)/2\rfloor$ crossings for every $s\ge3$, showing that the linear order of this local density bound is optimal.

papers.title: Linear bound for commuting matrix algebra II
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field, and let $A_1,\cdots,A_m$ be pairwise commuting $n\times n$ matrices. For $m\geq3$ and $n\geq2$, we prove \[ \dim_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{F}[A_1,\cdots,A_m] \leq \left\lceil C_m(n-1)\right\rceil \quad\text{with}\quad C_m=\frac{Γ(m)}{Γ((m+1)/2)^2}. \] In particular, three commuting matrices generate an algebra of dimension at most $2n-2$.

papers.title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation models represent items as sequences of discrete tokens known as semantic IDs. Existing approaches derive these identifiers using residual or hierarchical vector quantization, assuming that tokens carry independent semantic meaning across quantization levels. Revisiting this assumption, we argue that semantic IDs should behave as hierarchical paths where each token's meaning is conditioned on its prefix. This highlights a mismatch between conventional fixed-codebook quantization and the hierarchical structure implicitly learned by generative recommenders. Motivated by this insight, we propose Adaptive Silhouette Tree (AST), a top-down divisive clustering method that constructs semantic IDs as paths within a tree structure. Unlike prior methods with fixed branching factors, AST dynamically determines the number of branches at each node by maximizing the silhouette coefficient, enabling finer partitions in dense regions and compact groupings in homogeneous ones. We further introduce constrained variants that enforce minimum probability mass during splitting to improve supervision for long-tail items. Extensive experiments on five Amazon Review datasets of varying sizes and domains show that AST significantly outperforms strong baselines. These results demonstrate that aligning semantic ID construction with the inherent hierarchical structure of generative recommenders leads to more effective recommendations.

papers.title: Solar cycle variations of meridional flow and differential rotation in a non-kinematic dynamo model
papers.abstract: Flux transport dynamo models have emerged as the leading paradigm for explaining the observed solar cycle. However, most of these models are kinematic and axisymmetric. We develop a non-kinematic dynamo model by specifying large-scale flows, such as the differential rotation and meridional flow. Thus, our model does not require the $Λ$ effect or other parameterisations of turbulent transport to generate the large-scale flows; it only solves the fluctuating flows and thermodynamics. Our model is inherently 3D by construction, although it is currently operating in axisymmetric mode because the source for poloidal field generation (Babcock-Leighton $α$) is assumed to be axisymmetric. Our model reproduces solar-cycle variations in both the meridional flow and the differential rotation -- specifically, the torsional oscillation in some agreement with observations. The model naturally exhibits some variability in the solar cycle, even without incorporating stochastic fluctuations, offering a new methodology for modelling the non-kinematic solar dynamo in 3D.

papers.title: Dropping Tokens Without Dropping Them: Causal Attribution for Diabetic Retinopathy
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate whether attention-based attribution maps in a vision transformer provide causal explanations for diabetic retinopathy (DR) classification. We introduce a principled decomposition of attention into two attribution maps: the contribution ($c_t$), which satisfies the completeness axiom in explainable artificial intelligence (xAI), and the pull ($p_t$), which quantifies causal explanations. We define an identity relating $c_t$ and $p_t$ that characterizes when $c_t$ fails to capture causality. We test whether each map is causally faithful on the MAPLES-DR dataset by dropping/inserting tokens, and report Necessity ($N$), Sufficiency ($Su$), and Faithfulness Correlation ($FC$). The pull $p_t$ achieves the highest causal alignment ($FC = 0.53$, $N = 0.71\%$, $Su = 3.0\%$), outperforming Attention Rollout, Grad-CAM, and AttnLRP. Occlusion retains better sufficiency ($Su = 1.6\%$) but is about 800 times slower. Furthermore, on MAPLES-DR, $p_t$ achieves $70\%$ of the average precision (AP) of HRDecoder, a state-of-the-art supervised lesion segmentation model, despite the absence of pixel-level supervision. Together, these findings show that the pull $p_t$ and the contribution $c_t$ form computationally efficient attribution maps for reliable causal interpretation in safety-critical medical diagnostics. The code and demo are available at https://github.com/pramath-haritz/dr-xai.

papers.title: Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains
papers.abstract: For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.

papers.title: Suboptimality of Gaussian quadrature for Freud and logistic weights in weighted Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: We study the worst-case error of Gaussian quadrature for integrals over the real line weighted by Freud weights $\exp(-|x|^β)$ with $β>1$, and by the logistic density $\mathrm{e}^{-x}/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2$. The integrand functions are assumed to live in the $ρ$-weighted $L^2$-based Sobolev space of smoothness $α\in\mathbb{N}$. We prove that any linear quadrature using the $n$ Gaussian nodes, irrespective of the choice of quadrature weights, has a worst-case error bounded from below by a constant times $n^{-α(1-1/β)}$ for the Freud weights, and by a constant times $(\log n)^{-α}$ for the logistic weight. Our proof is based on three simple observations. First, the worst-case error of any linear quadrature is bounded from below in terms of the number of its nodes in a fixed interval. Second, the number of Gaussian nodes in such an interval is bounded from above by means of Christoffel functions. Third, Christoffel functions admit sharp lower bounds on such an interval. For the Freud weights with even integer exponents and for the logistic weight, all steps are proved in an elementary and self-contained way; for the logistic weight, we use explicit recurrence coefficients of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials. Our results provide a theoretical explanation, for integrands of finite smoothness, of the slow convergence of Gauss--Logistic quadrature observed in the literature. In contrast, for the logistic weight and for the Freud weights with even integer exponents, the Möbius-transformed trapezoidal rule attains the optimal rate $n^{-α}$. This rule does not depend on the smoothness $α$ and requires only point values of the integrand and the weight.

papers.title: Overcoming speed-accuracy trade-offs with medium-sized interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: Current machine-learned interatomic potentials offer a choice between small, fast models and large, expressive networks. This study demonstrates how an intermediate potential can approach the limit of transferable accuracy at the cost of the cheapest existing formalisms. Specifically, we model He-bearing W-Ta-Hf-Cr-V-Ti alloys with an atomic cluster expansion that learns the radial components of each polynomial as independent linear transforms and embeds numerous densities with learned exponents. While (near-)training loss appears largely a function of model size, the error on a distinct validation set is close to that of leading potentials with ten times more parameters. Taking advantage of the new structure, we develop optimized implementations that run more than an order of magnitude faster than the larger models and many times faster than smaller models with equivalent polynomials. The potential is trained on systematically enumerated small structures but generalizes to point and planar defects and can be extended to even more complex chemistries. As a demonstration, we simulate radiation-damage cascades in billion-atom systems for hundreds of thousands of timesteps.

papers.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
papers.abstract: We prove versions of (variations of) Erdős sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.

papers.title: Dashboard Remixing: Goal-oriented Organization and Enrichment of Visualizations and Insights
papers.abstract: Dashboard creation requires iteratively authoring multiple views and organizing them into a structured format. However, creators often struggle to step back and assess their own work for organization and refinement due to cognitive limitations. In this work, we propose a pipeline to provide computational support for self-reflection during the design process. Our pipeline automatically infers analytical objectives, discovers implicit patterns, and structures those patterns to surface coherent analytical pathways. It further enriches existing dashboard designs by generating complementary visualizations and aggregating natural language insights based on relationships across data entities (e.g., contrasting, drill-down, and relatedness) to reveal chart connections. Our rule-based pipeline provides objective, verifiable feedback, offering an external perspective while enabling creators to tell their own data stories. Four case studies and six expert interviews demonstrate how this approach helps creators reflect on organizational alternatives and surface hidden analytical opportunities in a principled way, reducing the cognitive burden while encouraging deeper analytical exploration.

papers.title: Safeguarding Agentic AI in Radiology Workflows: A Multimodel Evaluation of Rule-based and Large Language Model-based Verification
papers.abstract: Purpose: To estimate how often tool-using large language model (LLM) agents record clinically relevant false or unsupported information in simulated radiology documentation and how much safeguards applied before each action reduce these errors. Materials and Methods: In this simulation study (October 2026), 48 synthetic, radiologist-reviewed base scenarios covered finding communication, tumor board preparation and follow-up management. Forty-three also had a misleading-information variant (91 variants). Six LLM agents (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.8-27B) completed each variant with permissions only, deterministic rules, and rules plus a locally run LLM checker (1638 episodes). The primary outcome was at least one executed high-severity violation per episode. Risk differences were estimated per agent at base-scenario level and, exploratorily, pooled across agents, with analyses of document access and blocks. Results: With permissions only, 7.3%-27.1% of episodes had a high-severity violation (pooled across agents, 19.4%). Pooled, it was 16.7% with rules (-2.8 percentage points; 95% CI: -6.1, 0.5) and 13.2% with rules plus the LLM checker (-6.2; 95% CI: -9.5, -3.0). Adding the LLM checker to rules changed it by -3.5 (95% CI: -6.3, -0.7). No difference between agents was detected (P = .43), and task success did not decrease detectably. In misleading variants, agents opened the altered document in 83% of episodes regardless of error, and 58% of erroneous statements cited it. Most blocked actions (64%-68%) would not have caused a violation and were returned for revision. Conclusion: Layered safeguards reduced but did not prevent high-severity errors. Errors after misleading information reflected misjudged rather than missed information.

papers.title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
papers.abstract: We present \textit{Hydrograd} v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about $10^{-8}$ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7\,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2\,\%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6\,s for a forward run and 51\,s for a gradient.

papers.title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction
papers.abstract: This paper shifts the object of role engineering from human users to large language model (LLM) agents, and proposes PRISM to address the over-authorization that arises when an agent obtains full tool privileges through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). PRISM formulates whether a tool is necessary for a task as an intervenable causal proposition, and applies structured interventions in a sandbox to learn a counterfactual necessity model. It then compresses trajectories into discrete latent variables through an information bottleneck, and determines the number of roles from the knee of the rate-distortion curve. Finally, it formalizes pruning as a bilevel Stackelberg game, in which a generative flow network samples diverse near-optimal solutions. On three public benchmarks, AgentDojo, $τ$-bench and ToolEmu, PRISM compresses the number of authorized tools per role by 78.3%, attains a task success rate of 78.2%, reaches a counterfactual necessity accuracy of 88.7%, and lowers the blast radius to 15.9%.

papers.title: Axis-switching oscillations of elliptic scroll rings in excitable media
papers.abstract: Scroll waves in three-dimensional excitable media rotate around a filament that moves according to its local curvature. Using simulations of the Barkley model, we show that initially planar, elliptic scroll rings perform the axis-switching oscillation known from elliptic vortex rings in fluids: while the ring drifts along its axis, it buckles into a saddle, becomes planar again with interchanged axes, and repeats this cycle. The oscillation occurs for vanishing, positive, and negative filament tension. As predicted by a kinematic filament equation, its period scales approximately with the square of the ring radius and inversely with the drift coefficient. For our main model parameters, however, the oscillation is about 1.45 times slower than the linear prediction based on the drift of circular rings of the same size. A curvature-dependent drift coefficient accounts for a factor of about 1.25, while the remaining slowdown results mainly from a weaker coupling of out-of-plane to in-plane deformations, which a fourth-order rigidity term does not describe. In contrast, the Panfilov-Rudenko model and the Atri model of Ca$^{2+}$ waves follow the linear prediction within about 6%, showing that the slowdown depends on the kinetics.

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
papers.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) optimize circuit angles through repeated quantum-device evaluations, often facing vanishing gradients and high optimization costs. We ask whether a large language model (LLM) can write these angles directly. Extending *weight-space programming* from classical networks to quantum circuits, we provide a frontier LLM (\gpt) with the problem, circuit, and gate conventions. Its angles are executed exactly as written, without returning losses, gradients, or accuracy feedback. Across 139 requests, we test handwritten-digit classification, VQE ground-state estimation for spin chains and H$_2$, and MaxCut QAOA, comparing against random weights, classical optimization, and optimization initialized with LLM weights on the same circuit. When parameters have interpretable structure, the LLM matches or approaches the optimizer: it achieves 95--100\% of the energy spectrum on every VQE problem, derives the exact H$_2$ ground state in closed form, finds optimal depth-one QAOA angles for every graph, and reaches 93--96\% accuracy on digits 3 versus 8 with 12--18 hand-written weights, outperforming an optimizer trained on the same ten examples. Its weights are also strong warm starts: optimization reaches its best value after a median of one evaluation rather than hundreds. Allowed to design circuits, the LLM chooses data-dependent rotation chains encoding pixel importance in all 30 cases (one qubit for binary tasks, one chain per qubit for ten classes), reaching 65\% accuracy across ten digits. Yet the approach fails in opaque weight spaces: accuracy drops to chance when fixed circuits exceed 30 weights, while optimization improves. It is also sensitive to gate conventions: 6 of 42 QAOA replies reverse mixing-angle signs and fail. We release all prompts, replies, and scores.

papers.title: On Słociński-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
papers.abstract: The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a Słociński type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.

papers.title: Addressing Bias Early in the AI Lifecycle: Social Determinants of Health in Functional and Cognitive Assessment Labels of Nursing Home Residents
authors: Miguel A. Armengol de la Hoz
papers.abstract: Fairness in clinical artificial intelligence (AI) is usually evaluated after model training, yet bias can enter earlier in the AI lifecycle, during data collection and labelling. When routine clinical assessments serve as target variables, systematic differences in these labels across sociodemographic groups are carried into model development, validation and updating. This study addresses this early lifecycle stage by auditing labels from three standardised instruments used in residential care: the Barthel Index (BI), the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Global Deterioration Scale (GDS). Using electronic health records of 2,407 residents from 12 nursing homes in the Basque Country, Spain (2011-2021), we assessed four social determinants of health (SDoH) - sex, educational attainment, lifetime work activity and marital status - with two group fairness metrics, Disparate Impact (DI) and Statistical Parity Difference (SPD), computed for each outcome category with bootstrap confidence intervals. Disparities were found for all four attributes and across the three instruments: men, residents with intermediate education and never-partnered residents were more frequently classified in categories indicating preserved function or cognition. These disparities may reflect genuine differences in health status, measurement properties of the instruments, assessment practices or selective admission to residential care, and cannot be attributed to a single cause with the present design. Regardless of their origin, any model trained on these labels would inherit them, and they could persist through later lifecycle stages unless explicitly examined. These findings support pre-training label auditing as the first step of a continuous fairness assessment spanning model development, validation, deployment and updating.

papers.title: SU(2) Yang-Mills: Spectral Bounds, Vacuum Concentration, and Criteria for the Continuum Limit
papers.abstract: A continuum mass-gap argument must preserve nonzero renormalized states and a positive spectral estimate while the spatial cutoff is removed and physical volume grows. We develop quantitative results that separate these requirements. Gauge reduction, reflection positivity and attributed strong-coupling estimates give physical-transfer bounds with nontrivial local sectors. At fixed spatial cutoff and positive coupling, we construct subsequential infinite-volume physical-time dynamics from local history correlations, with nonconstant gauge-invariant observables. For finite spatial boxes, explicit bounds apply to the entire physical vacuum complement; finite-matrix criteria include all omitted representations. Vacuum concentration gives extensive entropy bounds, quantitative fidelity obstructions for hard electric cutoffs, and necessary growth of retained representation spaces. A sharper local comparison yields complete bounds on fixed discarded-link sectors, while collective projection and Schur estimates isolate the additional input needed for a volume-uniform gap. The work also certifies a finite three-link conditioning functional through Wilson coupling 0.354, with its physical interpretation conditional on the stated block-comparison hypotheses. Exact blocking, corrected effective-potential theorems and a representation-by-representation two-dimensional benchmark clarify which approximations preserve the relevant observables. Published glueball measurements retain their original attribution; their reanalysis and the reproduced winding-channel and replica studies have explicitly statistical scope. Complete derivations and reproducible calculations support a set of certified benchmarks and continuum transfer criteria. A nontrivial four-dimensional spatial-cutoff construction and a positive spectral bound along it are not established; no exact continuum mass is asserted.

papers.title: Ostinato: Fast CPU-GPU MoE Inference for Local Agents via Resident Experts in Every Forward Pass
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly run on workstations with a few consumer GPUs, where large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models keep part of their experts in host memory. With existing CPU-GPU engines, these agents get fast prefill or fast decode, not both: llama.cpp's expert cache skips forward passes of more than 32 tokens to keep the experts of decode cached, so an agent waits 2.1-2.8 s after each tool output, whereas its default layer placement shortens this wait but is 1.5-1.6$\times$ slower in decode. Our key insight is that a short prefill touches too many distinct experts to upload, yet sends 84% of its expert activations (routes) to a stable set of experts that fits in GPU memory. We present Ostinato, a CPU-GPU MoE inference engine that computes these experts on the GPUs in every forward pass without changing what the model computes. Short prefills split their routes, leaving fewer than one of a token's six routed experts per layer to the CPU; long prefills upload each distinct cold expert once; and each decode step runs as one fixed-shape CUDA graph per GPU. On real coding and customer-service agent sessions with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on four RTX 4090D GPUs, Ostinato is the fastest engine in both phases and finishes every session sooner than all six baselines. Against llama.cpp and KTransformers, it cuts the median wait after a tool output by 22-55% and finishes sessions 1.4-2.5$\times$ sooner.

papers.title: DriveFoundry: Co-Evolving Data and Model for Efficient Closed-Loop Iteration in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: A driving foundation model must learn reusable decision knowledge from rare critical events and apply it under strict runtime constraints. We introduce DriveFoundry, a closed-loop framework improving iteration efficiency under data and computation budgets by coupling structured causal data refinement with adaptive inference. The Data Engine builds traceable scene-candidate records linking scene evidence and factor-decision relations to candidate trajectories and outcome assessments. Candidate comparisons and counterfactual annotations clarify how scene factors affect behavioral feasibility and preference. Verified model failures guide VLM-assisted annotation and expert correction, refining training data and annotation systems. The model engine, Xiaomi-Drive-o1, unifies Perception, Causation, Action, World, and Value within a shared vision-language backbone to enable cross-task knowledge transfer. Block-wise latent refill passes candidate-specific evidence and predicted visual consequences between task blocks, connecting scene understanding, planning, and evaluation. A learned value-of-computation head selects tasks and allocates latent tokens based on expected benefit and cost, adapting inference to each decision. On PhysicalAI, the 9B model achieves the lowest ADE@1 across evaluated splits and horizons among tested models. In AlpaSim, it outperforms Alpamayo 1.5 across all metrics and achieves lower close-encounter and off-road rates than the 34B Alpamayo 2 Super, while trailing in progress and AlpaSim scores. For the 0.8B variant, joint training reduces 5 s minADE@6 by about 54% without altering the inference path or token budget. Adaptive inference matches full reasoning performance using only 28% of tokens. Real-vehicle tests confirm runtime feasibility, supporting a unified paradigm for learning from critical experience and dynamically allocating computation.

papers.title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
papers.abstract: Which representation should be probed in a transformer-based foundation model? Recent work shows that the standard practice of probing the final layer is often suboptimal, as intermediate layers can provide better features. Yet, representations are still largely studied along depth alone, treating each transformer block as an atomic unit. In this work, we analyze transformer representations layer by layer, module by module. Through more than 144,000 linear probing evaluations of vision foundation models (VFMs) and large language models (LLMs), we show that layer and module choices should be considered jointly: the best layer-module pair yields substantially larger gains over the final-layer residual stream than the best layer with the residual stream fixed. Moreover, module performance can vary substantially across layers, showing that useful representations cannot be characterized by depth alone. Building on these findings, we evaluate simple fixed probing strategies: the final-layer feedforward activation (Act@100) for vision and the second normalization layer at 60% depth (LN2@60) for language. These strategies improve over the probing baseline in a majority of evaluations and recover, on average, 42% and 86% of the gains from probing the best layer-module pair for vision and language, respectively. For VFMs, these gains increase with the transfer difficulty between pretraining and downstream data.

papers.title: Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space
papers.abstract: The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.

papers.title: Data Manipulation Attacks Against Machine Learning Integrated Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.abstract: There is a well-established body of work demonstrating that individual machine learning (ML) algorithms can be manipulated or deceived. However, in many real-world systems, multiple ML algorithms are composed to enable automated decision-making, particularly in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). Often such systems use a composition of vision, planning, and other ML models to affect their internal state and ultimate take actions in the physical world. While there is a huge literature on the (in)security of ML algorithms, it is not immediately clear how an attacker might leverage their ability to trick individual learners when attacking the composition as a whole. We develop methods for creating an attack policy (a mapping from state to attack) for a data-manipulating attacker affecting a CPS or other state-machine-based AI compositions. We describe our framework, a basic threat model and corresponding methods for computing an optimal attack policy, as well as planned extensions. The goal of this work-in-progress paper is to stimulate conversation and forge new collaborations regarding the security of compositional learning.

papers.title: Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations
papers.abstract: The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.

papers.title: Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
papers.abstract: We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.

papers.title: A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence
papers.abstract: AdamW is ubiquitous in deep learning, yet its behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze its dynamics through the lens of dynamical systems and show that AdamW admits an implicit fixed-point objective: its fixed points coincide with the stationary points of a constrained and regularized optimization problem. However, not all of these fixed points are stable under AdamW's dynamics, and stability depends sensitively on curvature, weight decay, and momentum parameters. Even in one-dimensional settings, equilibria may be unstable, and trajectories can exhibit persistent oscillations rather than convergence to them. We further extend the analysis to higher dimensions, deriving sufficient conditions for local stability of the continuous-time dynamics, and propose a convergent modification that preserves AdamW's fixed points. These results clarify what optimization problem AdamW is associated with, when its convergence can be expected, and how its dynamics could inspire more reliable optimizers.

papers.title: Boundary Mass in Feature Space as a Label-Budget Diagnostic for Representations
papers.abstract: Low-label transfer is often decided by a practical question: after a representation looks useful, how many labels are still needed to learn the downstream boundary? Transferability and probe-quality scores characterize global alignment, likelihood, margins, and calibration. Boundary-near target mass complements these diagnostics by measuring the ambiguous regions where scarce labels are most costly. We propose effective boundary complexity, a label-budget diagnostic for frozen representations and linear probes. It measures mass in a thin strip around the learned boundary and normalizes it by class balance, so dense ambiguous regions and predicted-class imbalance are both counted. We prove that, under a smooth representation map, density change and tangential surface change cancel at first order, leaving boundary-normal stretch or compression as the governing factor. This yields a cached-feature estimator that fits a probe on one split and counts independent held-out features near its boundary. Experiments support the diagnostic at three levels. Controlled transformations match the predicted law across 74 maps with 0.38% median relative error. On real frozen features, normal-direction changes move both measured boundary mass and label demand, while tangent controls preserve the first-order coefficient. A differentiable surrogate reduces measured complexity by 16-36% at matched top-1 utility. Finally, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet experiments support boundary mass as a second-stage diagnostic for near-tied representations. Five-way experiments show strong OvR-interface backbone-ranking agreement (Spearman 0.872), while acquisition experiments show high correlations between initial boundary mass and realized label budgets across three sampling policies (0.779-0.830). Code is available at https://github.com/qqaqq-code/boundary_mass.

papers.title: Extreme temperatures characterization of Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMT
papers.abstract: In this work, we fabricate and characterize ultra-wide bandgap Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs with Pt/Au gate under a wide temperature range of 20 K to 650 K. The devices retained robust modulation capability throughout the measurement, with excellent on/off ratio of 9.7 * 107 and 6.4 * 107 under 20 K and 650 K. The DC output IV measurement was performed, with Id,max of a device with Lsd = 9 μm measured to be 240 mA/mm and 120 mA/mm under 20 K and 650 K. In addition, low drain and leakage were observed in multiple devices, and the device robustness was evaluated under room temperature after the extreme temperature measurement with minimal degradation observed in Id,max and Rsheet. Moreover, transfer I-V characteristics of the Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs have also been studied, where a relatively small Vth shift was observed. TLM measurement and transconductance analysis both indicate the presence of weak temperature dependent scattering mechanisms in the device channel. The subthreshold swing (SS) was calculated and observed to increase parallelly to SSideal under investigated temperature, indicates a robust gate structure. Finally, the on/off ratio and Ig of the 9 μm Lsd device were benchmarked and compared favorably against other reported results. While the results offer insight into the extreme temperature performance of AlGaN channel HEMT with Al composition higher than 50%, it also establishes AlGaN channel HEMT as a promising candidate for extreme temperature electronic applications.

papers.title: Ultrawideband Polarization-Rotating Antenna for Enhanced Ground Penetrating Radar Detection
papers.abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents a powerful and widely adopted tool for nondestructive subsurface detection and imaging. To overcome the impaired detection performance caused by polarization mismatch in conventional single-channel GPR systems, this paper presents an innovative ultrawideband polarization-rotating (UPR) antenna that achieves rotating linear polarizations (LPs) by varying the source frequency for enhanced detection. The developed UPR antenna achieves a continuous polarization rotation from $0^\circ$ to $170^\circ$ across 1.2 to 3.2 GHz, as verified by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements. The antenna is subsequently integrated into a single-channel stepped-frequency GPR system and evaluated against targets of varying geometries in a sandy environment. Compared with a conventional fixed-LP GPR system, the UPR antenna-enabled GPR system delivers markedly more consistent detection performance across all target types, with particularly pronounced enhancements for polarization-sensitive targets. By enabling ultrawideband frequency-dependent polarization agility, the proposed GPR system enhances subsurface target detection while maintaining the simplicity and low cost of a single-channel measurement architecture.

papers.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
papers.abstract: We propose a music inpainting technique combining similarity matching and a diffusion-based generative model to replace large segments of audio recordings with suitable alternatives. The proposed hybrid method, Similarity-Guided Diffusion Posterior Sampling (SimDPS), retrieves candidate replacement segments from the wider signal based on contextual similarity and uses them to guide the diffusion process toward coherent reconstructions. Being model-agnostic, the framework is compatible with any pre-trained diffusion model operating in either the waveform or latent domain. Objective evaluations demonstrate that SimDPS outperforms widely adopted RePaint and DPS methods across acoustic features and neural-embedding distance metrics. Subjective evaluations on multi-genre music datasets confirm that SimDPS enhances perceptual plausibility compared to previous diffusion-based methods and demonstrates robustness to poorly matched similarity candidates. These findings pave the way for improved music restoration and context-aware audio editing.

papers.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
papers.abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.

papers.title: Hydra: Towards Transferable Multi-Task Learning on Temporal Graphs
papers.abstract: Real-world evolving networks are naturally modeled as temporal graphs (TGs), where capturing temporal dynamics is essential for predicting future graph properties that support downstream decision-making. Existing temporal graph methods have been developed primarily for single-task prediction, and little is known about their generalization across tasks or transfer to unseen networks. This leaves the challenge of multi-task graph property prediction in TGs largely open. We address this challenge by introducing Hydra, a novel architecture that integrates local connectivity features from temporal GNNs with a spectral learning module that captures global connectivity patterns. This design enables joint learning of local and global information under a multi-task objective. In multi-task classification, Hydra achieves an 8.9% relative gain in AUC over the strongest competitor. In multi-task regression, Hydra achieves competitive results in all three tasks, while obtaining the best results in two tasks with a 8.2% relative gain in MAE compared to the strongest baseline. Moreover, Hydra delivers these gains with a 22% reduction in training time compared to temporal transfer models. These results provide the first systematic evidence that multi-task transferable learning on temporal graphs is effective. By delivering consistent top-ranked performance, Hydra highlights multi-task training on temporal graphs as a promising direction toward adaptable foundation models for temporal graphs.

papers.title: From MNH to the Friedman--Komogortsev Method---which changes improve eye-movement classification?
papers.abstract: The Friedman-Komogortsev Method (FKM) is a rule-based classifier of fixations, saccades, and post-saccadic oscillations in 1000-Hz recordings, developed from the modified Nyström-Holmqvist algorithm (MNH) and used in several recent studies. FKM changes MNH in many ways at once: it centres MNH's Savitzky-Golay filter, adds a position-based test for whether an apparent post-saccadic oscillation continues the saccade, adds rejection tests, and changes several thresholds. We asked which of these changes alter agreement with human classification. Both algorithms were scored against twenty 26-s GazeBase reading recordings hand-classified by three trained raters, and each change was reverted in turn. FKM agreed better than MNH as MNH was used: saccade Cohen's kappa rose on all 20 recordings (median +0.034), and saccade boundaries moved from 2-3 ms late to the raters' sample. One change produced this: centring the filter, which removes a three-sample delay. Reinstating the delay returned FKM's saccade kappa to MNH's value, and centring MNH's filter alone made MNH match FKM on saccades and exceed it on post-saccadic events. The position-based test changed how saccades with several velocity peaks were divided, splitting 8% of rater-labelled "wavy" saccades into a saccade and a spurious oscillation against 39% for delay-corrected MNH. FKM's higher post-saccadic velocity floor traded recall for precision. The remaining changes had no measurable effect on these recordings. FKM's improvement over MNH is therefore a filter-alignment correction that MNH users can apply directly, plus a segmentation rule for multi-peak saccades.

papers.title: Giant gas permeance through a nanoporous crystalline 2D polymer
papers.abstract: Chemical separation processes represent one of the largest contributors to industrial energy consumption, underscoring the need for the most efficient separation strategies. Many separation processes rely on selective transport through porous media. In this context, two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising route to atomically precise porosity beyond the reach of traditional top-down fabrication, with the potential to enhance separation performance by increasing flow. Here we report measurements of gas transport through a one-molecule-thick layer of suspended, nanoporous poly(carboxyfantrip), a 2D polymer that has identical, nanometer-sized pores that cover nearly a quarter of the surface. This combination of ultimate thinness with high areal pore density gives normalized gas flows (permeances) that approach the effusion limit, three to four orders of magnitude above gas-sieving graphene membranes. We find that gases spanning nearly two orders of magnitude in molecular weight (H$_2$, He, N$_2$, CO$_2$, and SF$_6$) obey Graham's law and approach the ideal limit of non-interacting ballistic transport, despite strong, species-dependent gas-pore interactions. Simulations reproduce the measured permeances within experimental uncertainty and provide an atomistic picture of the transport process. This work demonstrates the potential of synthetic crystalline 2D polymers for chemical separation, water filtration, and quantum sensing.

papers.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
papers.abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

papers.title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
papers.abstract: World models allow autonomous vehicles to imagine the consequences of candidate actions before execution, but their reliability depends on the futures represented in their training data. We identify a survivorship bias in driving world models: because the futures recorded in prevailing driving datasets almost always end safely, existing models often imagine benign outcomes even when a collision is imminent. We introduce a neutral world model (NWM) that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective. The NWM more faithfully anticipates imminent collisions, while maintaining a low false collision rate and competitive generation quality in routine driving. We further use the model as an imagination engine for decision-making. Given multiple ego trajectories, the NWM predicts the future associated with each candidate, and a reward function evaluates these imagined outcomes before selecting an action. On challenging NAVSIM scenarios, this procedure selects the better trajectory more reliably than the baseline world model. Zero-shot experiments with real-world pedestrian dummy crossing data collected using an autonomous research vehicle further demonstrate transfer to unseen sensor observations. These results show that correcting survivorship bias enables world models to more faithfully reason about futures and support safety-critical decision-making in autonomous driving.

papers.title: Detecting Common Golfing Faults Using AI and Video-Derived Biomechanical Features
papers.abstract: Understanding how an athlete moves can improve both technique and safety, yet outside the laboratory technique is still assessed by eye. We present a pipeline that detects named golf swing faults from ordinary video, without markers or calibration. Instead of learning end to end, it tracks body pose and the clubhead in a body-centered frame, and classifies the biomechanical quantities a coach would measure, such as the height of the clubhead above the swing plane, with shallow boosted trees. We demonstrate the approach on two common faults, coming over-the-top (OTT) and early-extension (EE). On 160 swings and 143 swings from public sources it detects OTT and EE with a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.975 and 0.911 respectively. Because every feature is a biomechanical quantity a coach already uses, measured at a known phase of the downswing, each decision can be traced to the signals and the moments of the swing that drove it. The signals the model relies on most are the same ones a coach checks when diagnosing these faults. The pipeline processes phone video on a consumer laptop in seconds, so it could feasibly be developed into an app for golfers of all abilities and extended to other sports in which technique is judged against a biomechanical reference.

papers.title: Rules, Choice, and Chance: A Welfare Evaluation Framework for Student-School Matching
papers.abstract: Centralized student-school matching systems, adopted in the United States, Chile, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom, assign students to schools based on their submitted preference rankings and schools' priority policies. Yet welfare in these systems is typically measured through a narrow lens: a few aggregate statistics published by education authorities, such as the share of students unmatched or assigned to a top-ranked choice. A single aggregate cannot reveal how outcomes vary across students, or why. Welfare depends on three interacting forces: the rules policymakers set (algorithm, tie-breaking, list length limits); the choices students make (which and how many schools to rank); and chance (lottery draws and students' residential location). A rule that reduces unmatched rates may simultaneously lower top-ranked assignment rates for specific groups, and evaluating such trade-offs in advance is challenging because individual-level preference data are rarely available. We present Trace (Trade-offs in Rules, Agency, Chance, and Equity), an open-source framework that synthesizes individual-level preference profiles from aggregate data using mixtures of Mallows models and evaluates alternative rules across multiple welfare metrics, disaggregating outcomes by choice and chance. We apply Trace to two real-world systems: NYC high school matching, where we study minimum list length requirements, and Chilean school assignment, where we compare the current multiple tie-breaking rule with a counterfactual single tie-breaking rule. Both reveal substantial, heterogeneous welfare trade-offs, underscoring the value of simulation-based evaluation before implementing school choice reforms.

papers.title: Induced-Minor-Free Graphs Admit a Star-Based Separator of Size $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$
papers.abstract: Given an $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, we construct a balanced separator of $G$ consisting of $\tilde{O}(|V(H)|\sqrt{n})$ star subgraphs. Our result is an induced-minor-free analog of the famous separator theorem for $H$-minor-free graphs by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1990]. A key idea in our construction is a new decomposition of $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, analogous to the cop decomposition for $H$-minor-free graphs by Andreae [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 1986]. We also discuss several algorithmic applications of our result.

papers.title: Amortized Bayesian Experimental Design with In-Context Knowledge Conditioning
papers.abstract: Amortized Bayesian experimental design (BED) enables real-time design strategies by shifting acquisition cost offline, but existing methods remain tied to the prior and task distribution they were trained on and cannot exploit additional information available at deployment. We introduce in-context amortized BED with unified knowledge encoding (IMBUE), a BED framework that admits external knowledge at deployment through a unified in-context interface. IMBUE accepts two forms of such knowledge without retraining, namely user-specified prior knowledge and observations from previous instances of the experiment. Both are encoded as additional input tokens and processed in-context with the accumulated observations by a shared Transformer, and a learned reliability filter scores each external token against the observations and excludes inconsistent ones. Across four benchmarks, IMBUE accelerates early-stage information acquisition when the external knowledge is reliable, and remains close to the no-external baseline when it is not.

papers.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to radiative decays of fully heavy tetraquarks into quarkonia
papers.abstract: Within nonrelativistic QCD factorization, we calculate the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the decays of compact $T_{4Q}=QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ states ($Q=c,b$) into an $S$-wave quarkonium and a photon. Conservation of charge conjugation allows $T_{4Q}^{0^{++}}$ and $T_{4Q}^{2^{++}}$ to decay into $V_Q+γ$, with $V_c=J/ψ$ and $V_b=Υ$, while $T_{4Q}^{1^{+-}}$ can decay into $η_Q+γ$. At leading order in the heavy quark velocity expansion, we derive the short-distance coefficients for these decay widths in analytic form through $\mathcal{O}(αα_s^5)$, including the interference contribution between the two color configurations of $T_{4Q}^{0^{++}}$. All ultraviolet divergences at NLO are exactly canceled by renormalization. The NLO QCD corrections enhance the decay widths for $T_{4Q}^{2^{++}}\to V_Q+γ$ and $T_{4Q}^{1^{+-}}\toη_Q+γ$ by factors of approximately $2.94$ ($2.33$) and $2.22$ ($1.83$), respectively. The dependence on the renormalization scale $μ_R$ is reduced at NLO in most channels, although it remains sizable. Based on the NLO branching fractions, we estimate yields of order $10^6$--$10^7$ for $T_{4c}\to J/ψ+γ$ and $10^4$ for $T_{4c}\toη_c+γ$ in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13~\mathrm{TeV}$ with an integrated luminosity of $100~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The $J/ψ+γ$ channels can be investigated through $J/ψ\to\ell^+\ell^-$ in the $\ell^+\ell^-γ$ invariant-mass spectrum, complementing di-charmonium searches.

papers.title: Reaching Is Not Finding: Map-Anchored Visual Prompting for the Last Mile of Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) asks a drone to find an object described in natural language. The description usually locates the object relative to named landmarks, such as streets and buildings. We observe that current navigators often bring the drone close to the target and then stop at the wrong place: they reach the target without finding it. This gap is shared by navigators of very different designs, from imitation learners to a fine-tuned 7B vision-language model. A simple test reveals the cause. When we replace the target object in the instruction with another one next to the same landmarks, no navigator goes to it, and most stop where they did before. Navigators learn to reach the landmarks, not to identify the described object. We therefore propose MAP-VP, a plug-and-play module for the last step. After any navigator stops, MAP-VP draws the landmarks named in the instruction onto the drone's current view, using the landmark outlines that the benchmark provides on a map. A fine-tuned 4B vision-language model then locates the target relative to these landmarks. The training data are generated automatically from the benchmark annotations. Neither drawing the landmarks nor fine-tuning helps much alone, but together they are highly effective. Without retraining any navigator, MAP-VP significantly improves all six navigators we test on CityNav. It roughly doubles the success rate of the two strongest trained navigators, raising HETT from 25.9% to 54.6% and FlightGPT from 24.2% to 48.9%, whereas CityNav's official detector-based last step adds less than two points to HETT.

papers.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

papers.title: Amortized Cell-Probe Lower Bounds for Dynamic Boolean Problems
papers.abstract: We prove the first unconditional amortized $Ω\big((\log N/\log\log N)^2\big)$ cell-probe lower bound for a Boolean dynamic problem. For insert-only multiphase Disjointness with $N$ query sets over $[N]$ and word size $w=Θ(\log N)$, a fixed distribution of interleaved insertions and queries forces this expected average cost per operation, excluding preprocessing. The bound allows sufficiently small constant error for each query of every fixed legal sequence and imposes no restriction on individual operation costs. It transfers to incremental directed reachability, incremental subgraph connectivity, and fully dynamic triangle detection. We also prove $t_q=Ω\big((\log N/\log(t_uw))^2\big)$ for amortized insertion time $1\le t_u=N^{o(1)}$ and expected query time $t_q$, when the number of insertions before the final query is not announced in advance. We reach the quadratic-logarithmic scale with bounded error by combining interleaving with the 2.5-round communication framework [Ko26a, Ko26b] and controlling errors among accepted simulations.

papers.title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference
papers.abstract: Lookup-table (LUT)-based neural networks (NNs) offer a compelling path to ultra-low-latency inference on FPGAs. However, existing LUT-based neural networks have largely been restricted to MLP-style topologies, leaving structured vision and audio tasks underexplored. We present ConvLUT, a family of fully unrolled LUT-mappable convolutional architectures targeting the MLPerf Tiny benchmarks. It is comprised of a standard convolutional model built around a hierarchical tree of LUTs and a depthwise separable model following the MobileNet design philosophy. These architectures are enabled by four key contributions: a unified LUT-based convolutional framework supporting standard, depthwise, and pointwise convolutions under explicit fan-in constraints; a LUT-tree that addresses the $k^2c$ receptive field dimensionality bottleneck; a channel-partitioned LUT pooling layer that replaces conventional spatial pooling; and a hardware-aware iterative pruning strategy for stable convergence at scale. Evaluated on CIFAR-10, Visual Wake Words, and Keyword Spotting, ConvLUT achieves competitive accuracy with fully unrolled inference latencies below $\sim 50$ ns. On CIFAR-10 it reaches at least a $8844\times$ latency reduction over non-logic-based prior implementations, and outperforms existing MLP-style LUT-based models on the same task by at least $20$ pp in test accuracy.

papers.title: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: An LLM agent that reads untrusted content, such as an email or a web page, may follow instructions hidden in it. Noninterference is too strong for such agents, since a useful agent lets untrusted content influence what it does and may disclose the user's data by design, and declassification needs a release policy written for each task. We instead state security relative to a reference agent, which runs the same plan under the same runtime monitor with a model that never obeys untrusted content. An agent is relatively secure if every leak it has is a leak the reference already has. Our framework, PlanTERS, instantiates relative security, a notion from speculative execution, with a small agent language in which the attacker chooses how the model follows instructions, a composition with runtime monitors, and attacker models that differ in what they observe. A fence theorem shows that revoking injectable tools at the first untrusted read, and never granting them back, makes every plan relatively secure at the event level on finite runs, for every model behaviour in which each injection is a single call and the model obeys on a schedule fixed in advance; with a fairness condition, this extends to possibly infinite runs. We prove or refute relative security for agents with fences, budgets, approvals, loops and dual LLMs, in Isabelle/HOL.

papers.title: A 40 Gbit/s FPGA-based RoCEv2 transport for detector readout: development and performance
papers.abstract: Recording the complete input of a detector trigger allows trigger algorithms to be replayed and studied offline. For the BESIII main drift chamber (MDC), this requires moving tens of Gbit/s from trigger FPGAs into server memory without loss. Remote direct memory access over Converged Ethernet (RoCEv2) lets commercial network adapters write such data into host memory. Detector readout also needs record boundaries that the receiver can check, replay from a verified copy, and host buffers that are reused only after consumption. We present a 40 Gbit/s FPGA RoCEv2 transport that provides these functions. Records are aggregated into CRC32C-checked blocks, and unacknowledged data are kept in DDR memory and verified before replay. Acknowledgment-aware retention writes to DDR only the data that are not acknowledged in time. The transport runs on a ZCU102 board and on the 9U VME Trigger Core Board (TCB). With records of 128 B to 4 KiB it comes within 0.4% of the packetization limit of the link, delivering 36.9 Gbit/s of payload at a path MTU of 1024 B, and its block latency is set by the time needed to fill a block. On a direct link, acknowledgment-aware retention cuts DDR writes for large blocks from 106% to 0.03% of the payload, and injected DDR access errors stay within their queue pair. On the TCB, three 16.4 TB transfers through two switches lost at most five packets each, all recovered by replay. An installation at the MDC is under test.

papers.title: Data-informed Adaptation of Foundation Models for Causal Effect Estimation
papers.abstract: Due to the fundamental problem of causal inference -- the impossibility of observing counterfactual outcomes -- there is always a gap between the training goal (outcome, propensity) and the inference target (CATE, ATE). Traditional causal effect estimation revolves around setting assumptions, selecting identification strategies, and choosing causal estimators, while more recently, Causal Foundation Models (CFMs), built on Prior-Data-Fitted Networks (PFNs), ease this process by pretraining on massive synthetic prior datasets. Despite their success, such amortization makes causal inference less transparent, obscuring which assumptions the model implicitly relies on for a given dataset. The high diversity of real-world data-generating processes (DGPs) and Structural Causal Models (SCMs) makes it hard to know, a priori, which causal inference strategy is compatible with a given dataset. In this work, we focus on this compatibility between an observational dataset and method-specific assumptions, and find that geometric characteristics of data embeddings -- specifically, the variogram -- provide a useful signal of whether a given causal estimation strategy is appropriate. We develop MoE-Learner, a mixture-of-causal-experts framework that embeds a dataset under multiple assumption-specific views and uses the variogram as a counterfactual-free router to assess each expert's validity. Rather than eliminating causal assumptions, this shifts their validation from a fixed, a priori choice to a criterion that can be checked directly from data geometry. MoE-Learner achieves the best average rank on benchmark datasets (IHDP, ACIC, Lalonde). Being orthogonal to (causal) foundation models, our method builds a bridge from data characteristics to causal estimation strategy rather than proposing another CFM.

papers.title: AgentCT: A Vision-Language Agent for Universal CT Imaging
papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) restoration methods often use a single network for low-dose CT (LDCT), sparse-view CT (SVCT), and metal artifact reduction (MAR), despite the distinct physics of these degradations. We propose AgentCT, a vision-language agent that identifies the degradation and routes images to task-specific restoration models. A LoRA-adapted Qwen3-VL-4B controller predicts degradation type and severity, selects a specialist, and reassesses the restored image. The LDCT specialist uses an image-domain diffusion model, whereas the SVCT and MAR specialists combine projection-domain correction, data consistency, differentiable filtered back-projection, and image refinement. We evaluated the controller and specialists separately on patient-disjoint Mayo 2020 abdominal CT data across three severity levels for each degradation. The controller achieved 95.7% accuracy for degradation type and 93.9% for severity, with a 100% JSON parse rate. Using ground-truth degradation labels for routing, AgentCT achieved an overall PSNR/SSIM of 46.18 dB/0.984, compared with 44.93 dB/0.976 for AMIR and 44.29 dB/0.979 for TAMP, and attained the highest PSNR in all nine settings. For SVCT, its dual-domain specialist achieved 46.04 dB with 4.2 million parameters, compared with 44.43 dB for single-task AMIR and 43.57 dB for all-in-one AMIR with 23.5 million parameters. These results support degradation-specific CT restoration with controller-based model selection; evaluation under automatic routing and on independent clinical data remains necessary. Code is available at https://github.com/hao1635/AgentCT.

papers.title: Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism
papers.abstract: Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper separates their program into the working hypothesis H, that Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra, and the claim P placed on top of it, that language and physics obey the same principle, and examines the validity of H. MCB employs two coproducts in formulating Merge, corresponding to two different translations of movement (Internal Merge): $Δ_d$, which deletes the lower copy, and $Δ_c$, which leaves a trace. MCB uses the former in syntax and the latter at the syntax-semantics interface, but $Δ_d$ is not coassociative, and $Δ_c$ is not connected under the gradings MCB gives and, moreover, not coassociative as long as the labels of traces are retained. Consequently, MCB's algebra is not a Hopf algebra, and the Birkhoff factorization is not a consequence of the Hopf-algebra theorem but of a weaker statement that requires neither coassociativity nor connectedness. There are four ways to recover a Hopf algebra, but none of them can distinguish different traces, and hence none is compatible with Heim-Kratzer-style formal semantics, which reads traces as indexed variables. Thus H does not hold at present, and under the current formulation, making Minimalism a Hopf algebra and preserving its connection with formal semantics are mutually exclusive. Finally, we indicate three directions in which algebraic Minimalism may proceed.

papers.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
papers.abstract: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

papers.title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires representations that capture both scene geometry and its evolution during interaction. Existing approaches have largely treated these two aspects separately. World action models capture such dynamics by coupling action prediction with future video generation, but their reliance on iterative diffusion or rectified-flow inference leads to high computational cost, while their representations lack explicit spatial structure. Explicitly modeling scene geometry typically requires auxiliary modules that increase both parameter count and computational cost. Conversely, geometry-centric policies primarily recover observed spatial structure and often lack explicit supervision for anticipating future geometric changes during interaction. To address these limitations, we introduce ForeAct, which repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency control. ForeAct directly processes the clean latent of the current observation in one forward pass, eliminating future-frame synthesis and iterative denoising while retaining the backbone's pretrained spatiotemporal priors. Rather than introducing a separate geometry backbone, ForeAct uses learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth to shape the shared video representation through bidirectional self-attention. This compact interface turns the spatial knowledge already encoded in the backbone into a future-aware representation for action generation, with little parameter overhead. The lightweight geometry readout is used only during training and removed at deployment, enabling low-latency, geometry-aware control without depth input or an external geometry backbone. Without additional large-scale pretraining, ForeAct achieves 96.6% average success on LIBERO, 63.5% on SimplerEnv-Bridge, and a 74.4% success rate across 90 real-world rollouts.

papers.title: JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The performance of language agents depends jointly on model weights and the harness. Optimizing either alone can be constrained by the other component, limiting overall performance gains. Our analysis of naive alternating training reveals progressive incompatibility between the model and harness, which increasingly interferes with task execution and may also undermine model training, leading to performance degradation. To coordinate the evolution of models and harnesses, we introduce JoMoHa, to our knowledge the first framework to jointly train an executable harness generation policy and a task execution policy through reinforcement learning. JoMoHa outperforms the evaluated weight-only and harness-only baselines and achieves the highest success rates among the evaluated methods on ALFWorld, WebShop, and DBBench, averaging 70.3% and reaching 97.0% on ALFWorld. By learning both task execution and runtime improvement from its own generated trajectories, JoMoHa performs recursive self-improvement (RSI).

papers.title: EVAX: Towards a Practical, Pro-active & Adaptive Architecture for High Performance & Security
papers.abstract: This paper provides an end-to-end solution to defend against known microarchitectural attacks such as speculative execution attacks, fault-injection attacks, covert and side channel attacks, and unknown or evasive versions of these attacks. Current defenses are attack specific and can have unacceptably high performance overhead. We propose an approach that reduces the overhead of state-of-art defenses by over 95%, by applying defenses only when attacks are detected. Many current proposed mitigations are not practical for deployment; for example, InvisiSpec has 27% overhead and Fencing has 74% overhead while protecting against only Spectre attacks. Other mitigations carry similar performance penalties. We reduce the overhead for InvisiSpec to 1.26% and for Fencing to 3.45% offering performance and security for not only spectre attacks but other known transient attacks as well, including the dangerous class of LVI and Rowhammer attacks, as well as covering a large set of future evasive and zero-day attacks. Critical to our approach is an accurate detector that is not fooled by evasive attacks and that can generalize to novel zero-day attacks. We use a novel Generative framework, Evasion Vaccination (EVAX) for training ML models and engineering new security-centric performance counters. EVAX significantly increases sensitivity to detect and classify attacks in time for mitigation to be deployed with low false positives (4 FPs in every 1M instructions in our experiments). Such performance enables efficient and timely mitigations, enabling the processor to automatically switch between performance and security as needed.

papers.title: TID System for Speech-COSER Challenge 2026: ASR Track
papers.abstract: We describe the system submitted by Telefónica Innovación Digital to the Speech-COSER Challenge 2026, which features spontaneous speech from elderly speakers recorded in rural Spain. For ASR, we perform CTC-based pseudo-forced alignment scores audio-text match quality to guide a two-stage LoRA curriculum, followed by post-hoc magnitude pruning of the LoRA matrices to enhance generalization. An ensemble of seven systems combined via ROVER achieves 36.25\% unnormalized and 22.17\% normalized WER.

papers.title: Graph-regularized synthetic control for spatial panels with post-only treated locations
papers.abstract: Spatial policy panels can contain treated locations that are observed only after an intervention and therefore have no pre-treatment outcome history. Without a pre-treatment trajectory to match, choosing donor weights for such post-only locations requires an additional source of information. We propose Graph-SCM, which estimates donor weights jointly across treated locations and encourages geographically neighboring locations to use similar donor combinations. GeoEco-SCM keeps the same geographic graph but adjusts the strength of its existing edges using pre-treatment economic similarity. Both methods handle complete, partial, and absent histories within one convex weight-estimation problem. Monte Carlo experiments compare them with covariate-balanced synthetic controls, equally weighted donor averages, ordinary synthetic control where estimable, and nonseparable spatio-temporal imputation and direct prediction. No method dominates. Graph-based borrowing improves on covariate balancing in several settings, but a selective-coverage design favors covariate balancing. Economic adjustment helps when geography alone misses relevant donor relationships. The results support graph regularization as a way to extend synthetic-control coverage when connected locations share similar donor representations, with its usefulness depending on the structure of the available information.

papers.title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
papers.abstract: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section.
